# Modem Pay documentation

# Modem Pay documentation
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/introduction

Modem Pay is one API for getting paid and paying people in The Gambia. Your customers pay with **Wave, Afrimoney, QMoney, APS, Yonna or card**. You get one balance, one dashboard and one set of webhooks.

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Quickstart" icon="rocket" href="/documentation/quickstart">
    Take your first test payment in about five minutes.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Choose an integration" icon="signs-post" href="/documentation/payments/overview">
    No code, a few lines of HTML, or a full API. Pick what fits.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## Get paid

<CardGroup cols={3}>
  <Card title="Payment links" icon="link" href="/documentation/core/payment-links">
    Share a link on WhatsApp, SMS or social media. No website needed.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Pay button" icon="hand-pointer" href="/documentation/payments/drop-in">
    One HTML tag adds a payment button to any page.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Checkout pop-up" icon="window-restore" href="/documentation/payments/modem-inline">
    Customers pay without leaving your site.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Payment intents" icon="code" href="/documentation/payment-intents/overview">
    Full control from your server: create, charge, verify, cancel.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Direct charge" icon="mobile-screen" href="/documentation/payment-intents/direct-charge">
    Send the payment request straight to the customer's wallet.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Invoices" icon="file-invoice" href="/billing/invoices/introduction">
    Itemised bills with due dates, reminders and overdue tracking.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Virtual terminals" icon="qrcode" href="/documentation/virtual-terminal">
    A QR code for each counter, with WhatsApp alerts for staff.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Stablecoins" icon="coins" href="/documentation/stablecoins/overview">
    Accept USDT and USDC, or turn them into dalasi.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Coupons" icon="ticket" href="/documentation/core/coupons">
    Percentage or fixed discounts with limits and expiry dates.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## How it works

<Steps>
  <Step title="Build in test mode">
    Every account starts with test keys (`sk_test_`, `pk_test_`). Nothing you do with them moves real money.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Get verified">
    Submit your business documents (KYC) from the dashboard.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Go live">
    Swap your test keys for live keys (`sk_live_`, `pk_live_`). Your code stays the same.
  </Step>
</Steps>

See [Test mode and going live](/documentation/test-mode) for the full checklist.

## Libraries and tools

| | Install |
| --- | --- |
| Node.js | `npm install modem-pay` |
| Python | `pip install modempay` |
| PHP | `composer require modempay/modempay-php` |
| Laravel | [Laravel package](/laravel/quickstart) |
| WordPress | [WooCommerce plugin](/plugins/woocommerce) and [payment form](/plugins/payment-form) |
| CLI | `npm install -g modem-pay-cli` |

Prefer raw HTTP? Every SDK call is a plain JSON request to `https://api.modempay.com/v1` with your secret key in the `Authorization` header.

<Tip>
  Using an AI assistant? Point it at [docs.modempay.com/llms.txt](https://docs.modempay.com/llms.txt), or use the menu at the top of any page to copy it or open it in ChatGPT, Claude or Cursor.
</Tip>

Need help? Email [info@modempay.com](mailto:info@modempay.com).

# Quickstart Guide
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/quickstart

Modem Pay lets you accept **Wave, Afrimoney, QMoney, APS, Yonna and card** payments through one integration. You build once, and your customers pay with whichever method they prefer.

This page takes you from sign-up to your first test payment.

## Before you start

| You need                        | Where to get it                                           |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| A Modem Pay account             | [Sign up on the dashboard](https://merchant.modempay.com) |
| Your API keys                   | Dashboard, under API keys                                 |
| A URL to send customers back to | Your website or app                                       |

<Note>
  Everything on this page works in **test mode**. No real money moves until you
  [go live](#go-live).
</Note>

## Accept your first payment

<Steps>
  <Step title="Create your account">
    Register on the [Modem Pay dashboard](https://merchant.modempay.com). This short video walks you through it:

    <iframe
      width="100%"
      height="400"
      src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/xY_ysj40diU?si=5_BdUUsXZmfnIUQu"
      title="Creating a Modem Pay account"
      frameborder="0"
      allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share"
      referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
      allowfullscreen
    ></iframe>

  </Step>

  <Step title="Copy your API keys">
    You get two kinds of keys from the dashboard:

    | Key | Starts with | Use it |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Secret key | `sk_test_` / `sk_live_` | On your **server only**, with the SDKs and API |
    | Public key | `pk_test_` / `pk_live_` | In your **website**, with HTML Checkout |

    <Warning>
    Never put your secret key in a website, mobile app or public repository. Anyone with it can act on your account.
    </Warning>

  </Step>

  <Step title="Create a payment">
    From your server, create a **payment intent** with the amount to charge. Modem Pay returns a `payment_link`.

    <CodeGroup>
    ```javascript nodejs
    import ModemPay from "modem-pay";

    const modempay = new ModemPay("sk_test_...");

    const intent = await modempay.paymentIntents.create({
      amount: 450,
      return_url: "https://yoursite.com/payment/success",
      cancel_url: "https://yoursite.com/payment/cancelled",
    });

    console.log(intent.data.payment_link);
    ```

    ```python python
    from modempay import ModemPay

    modem_pay = ModemPay(api_key="sk_test_...")

    intent = modem_pay.payment_intents.create(params={
        "amount": 450,
        "return_url": "https://yoursite.com/payment/success",
        "cancel_url": "https://yoursite.com/payment/cancelled",
    })

    print(intent["data"]["payment_link"])
    ```

    ```php php
    use ModemPay\ModemPay;

    $modemPay = new ModemPay('sk_test_...');

    $payment = $modemPay->paymentIntents()->create([
        'amount' => 450,
        'return_url' => 'https://yoursite.com/payment/success',
        'cancel_url' => 'https://yoursite.com/payment/cancelled',
    ]);

    echo $payment->data->payment_link;
    ```
    </CodeGroup>

    Amounts are in **GMD**, and the minimum is **10 GMD**.

  </Step>

  <Step title="Send your customer to pay">
    Redirect the customer to the `payment_link`. They choose how to pay and complete the payment on Modem Pay's checkout.

    When they finish, they come back to your `return_url`. If they cancel, they go to your `cancel_url`.

  </Step>

  <Step title="Confirm the payment with webhooks">
    Add your webhook URL in the dashboard. Modem Pay notifies your server when a payment changes, for example `charge.succeeded` or `charge.cancelled`.

    <Tip>
    Mark orders as paid **from the webhook**, not from the redirect. Customers sometimes close the page before they get back to your `return_url`, but the webhook still arrives.
    </Tip>

  </Step>
</Steps>

That's it. You've accepted a test payment.

---

## Choose how to integrate

The steps above use an **SDK**. If you'd rather not write server code, use **HTML Checkout**.

|             | SDK / API                                                 | HTML Checkout                   |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Best for    | Apps and sites with a backend                             | Simple websites, quick launches |
| Code needed | Server code                                               | A single HTML form              |
| Key used    | Secret key (`sk_`)                                        | Public key (`pk_`)              |
| Control     | Full: payment intents, split payments, transfers, refunds | Collect payments                |

### HTML Checkout

Add a form to your page that posts the payment details to Modem Pay. When the customer clicks **Pay Now**, they're taken to checkout.

Try it here:

<iframe
  height="400"
  width="100%"
  title="Modem Pay HTML Checkout"
  src="https://codepen.io/mercury-sms/embed/WNVLZwe?default-tab=html%2Cresult"
  frameborder="0"
  allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share; fullscreen"
  referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
  allowfullscreen
></iframe>

The form posts to `https://test.checkout.modempay.com/api/pay` with these fields:

| Field            | Required    | Description                                      |
| ---------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `public_key`     | Yes         | Your public key (`pk_test_...` or `pk_live_...`) |
| `amount`         | Yes         | Amount in GMD, at least 10                       |
| `currency`       | No          | `GMD`                                            |
| `return_url`     | Recommended | Where the customer goes after paying             |
| `cancel_url`     | Recommended | Where the customer goes if they cancel           |
| `customer_name`  | No          | Prefills checkout                                |
| `customer_email` | No          | Prefills checkout                                |
| `customer_phone` | No          | Prefills checkout                                |
| `metadata`       | No          | Your own data, e.g. an order ID.                 |

Example of what Modem Pay receives:

```json
{
  "public_key": "pk_test_...",
  "amount": "450",
  "currency": "GMD",
  "customer_name": "Zypheron Kade",
  "customer_email": "usr@example.com",
  "customer_phone": "7000001",
  "return_url": "https://yoursite.com/payment/success",
  "cancel_url": "https://yoursite.com/payment/cancelled",
  "metadata": { "order_id": "1042" }
}
```

Redirects and webhooks work exactly as in the SDK flow above.

---

## Go live

When your test payments work:

<Steps>
  <Step title="Complete KYC">
    Submit your business verification from the dashboard. This is required
    before you can accept real payments.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Switch to live mode">
    Once KYC is approved, switch to **live mode** in the dashboard and replace
    your `test` keys with your `live` keys.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Run one real payment">
    Make a small real payment and check that your webhook marks the order as
    paid.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Note>
  Test and live are kept separate. Payments and sub-accounts created in test
  mode don't exist in live mode, and the reverse.
</Note>

# SDKs and libraries
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/installation

## Prerequisites

Before installing, make sure you have the following:

- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) (v16 or higher; the CLI needs v18)
- [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/)
- [Python](https://www.python.org/) (at least 3.8)
- [PHP](https://www.php.net/) (at least 8.1)
- [Composer](https://getcomposer.org/) (for PHP dependency management)

---

## Install the Modem Pay SDK
To get started, install the SDK in your Node.js or Python project:

<CodeGroup>
```bash npm
npm install modem-pay
```
```bash python
pip install modempay
```
```bash php
composer require modempay/modempay-php
```
</CodeGroup>
---

## Initialize the SDK

To authenticate requests, instantiate the SDK with your **Modem Pay secret API key**:

<CodeGroup>
```ts typescript
import ModemPay from "modem-pay";

const modempay = new ModemPay("YOUR_MODEM_PAY_API_KEY");

const intent = await modempay.paymentIntents.create({ amount: 450 });

console.log(intent.data.payment_link);
```

```python python
from modempay import ModemPay

modem_pay = ModemPay(api_key="YOUR_MODEM_PAY_API_KEY")

intent = modem_pay.payment_intents.create(params={"amount": 450})

print(intent["data"]["payment_link"])
```

```php php
use ModemPay\ModemPay;

$modemPay = new ModemPay('YOUR_MODEM_PAY_API_KEY');

$payment = $modemPay->paymentIntents()->create(['amount' => 450]);

echo $payment->data->payment_link;
```
</CodeGroup>

<Warning>
🔐 Never expose your secret API key on the frontend or in public repositories.
</Warning>

---

## Get Your API Key

1. Log in to [modempay.com](https://merchant.modempay.com).
2. Go to **Developers** → **API Keys**.
3. Generate or copy your secret key.
4. Use this key when initializing the SDK.

---

## Install the Modem Pay CLI (optional)

To receive test webhooks on your machine and send sample events:

```bash bash
npm install -g modem-pay-cli
```

Use `modempay listen` to test webhooks locally and `modempay trigger` to simulate events.

<Tip>
See [Modem Pay CLI](/documentation/cli) for everything it can do.
</Tip>

---

# API keys
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/authentication

Every request to the Modem Pay API needs a **secret key**. You create and manage keys in the dashboard under **Developers → API keys**.

## Your two kinds of key

| Key | Looks like | Where it goes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Secret key** | `sk_test_…` / `sk_live_…` | Your server only. Used by the SDKs and the API. |
| **Public key** | `pk_test_…` / `pk_live_…` | Your website. Used by the pay button, checkout pop-up and HTML Checkout. |

`test` keys only touch test data. `live` keys move real money. A test key can't see live data, and a live key can't see test data.

<Warning>
  Never put a secret key in a website, mobile app or public repository. Anyone with it can act on your account. If one leaks, [roll it](#roll-a-key) straight away.
</Warning>

<Note>
  Modem Pay stores only a hash of each secret key. You see the full key **once**, when you create it. Save it somewhere safe, like your server's environment variables. If you lose it, roll the key to get a new one.
</Note>

## Make a request

Send the secret key as a bearer token:

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs
import ModemPay from "modem-pay";

const modempay = new ModemPay(process.env.MODEMPAY_SECRET_KEY);
```

```python python
import os
from modempay import ModemPay

modem_pay = ModemPay(api_key=os.environ["MODEMPAY_SECRET_KEY"])
```

```php php
use ModemPay\ModemPay;

$modemPay = new ModemPay(getenv('MODEMPAY_SECRET_KEY'));
```

```bash cURL
curl https://api.modempay.com/v1/balances \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```
</CodeGroup>

## Full-access and restricted keys

A **full-access** key can call every endpoint. That's convenient, but risky: if it leaks, someone could send payouts from your balance.

A **restricted** key can only do what you allow. Give each system its own restricted key with just the permissions it needs. For example, your website's checkout only needs to create payments. It never needs to send money.

When you create a restricted key in the dashboard you can set:

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Permissions" icon="list-check">
    Pick exactly which resources it can read or change.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Expiry" icon="clock">
    1 day, 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, 1 year, never, or a date you choose.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Allowed IP addresses" icon="network-wired">
    Up to 20 IP addresses or ranges. Requests from anywhere else are refused.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Payout limits" icon="gauge">
    A maximum per payout and per day, for keys that can send money.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

You can have up to **5** active full-access keys and **20** active restricted keys per account and mode.

### Permissions

Each permission is a resource and an access level, like `payments:write`. A `write` permission includes `read` for the same resource.

| Permission | `read` lets the key… | `write` lets the key… |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `payments` | View payment intents and payment methods available at checkout | Create, charge, confirm and cancel payment intents |
| `transactions` | View transactions | — |
| `refunds` | — | Refund customers **(moves money)** |
| `transfers` | View payouts, bulk payouts, fees and payout channels | Send and reverse payouts **(moves money)** |
| `balance` | View balances | — |
| `customers` | View customers and their saved payment methods | Create, update and delete customers |
| `payment_methods` | View payment methods and mandates | Create, attach and detach payment methods |
| `payment_links` | View payment links | Create, update and delete payment links |
| `invoices` | View invoices | Create, edit, send and mark invoices as paid |
| `coupons` | View coupons | Create, update and delete coupons |
| `sub_accounts` | View sub-accounts and groups | Create, update and deactivate them **(changes where money goes)** |
| `terminals` | View virtual terminals and download posters | Create, update and delete terminals |
| `ramps` | View stablecoin payments and conversions, get quotes | Create stablecoin payments and conversions **(moves money)** |
| `webhooks` | — | Trigger test webhook events |

### Ready-made sets

The dashboard offers three starting points:

| Preset | Includes | Good for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Read only** | Every `read` permission | Reporting, accounting, dashboards |
| **Accept payments** | `payments`, `payment_links` and `customers` (write), plus `transactions` and `balance` (read) | Website and app checkouts |
| **Payments and transfers** | `payments` and `transfers` (write), plus `transactions` and `balance` (read) | Systems that collect and pay out |

### Payout limits

On a key that can send money, you can set:

- `per_transfer`: the most a single payout can be.
- `daily`: the most the key can send in total each day.

For bulk payouts, every item counts. If a request would go over a limit, it's refused with `per_transfer_limit_exceeded` or `daily_transfer_limit_exceeded`, and nothing is sent.

## IP allowlists

There are two levels:

- **Per key:** set when you create the key. Applies to that key only.
- **Per account:** set in the dashboard. Applies to every key on that account and mode.

A request must pass both. Ranges use CIDR, like `203.0.113.0/24`.

## Roll a key

Rolling replaces a key with a new one. You choose how long the old key keeps working, from 0 hours up to 7 days (24 hours by default), so you can update your servers without downtime. The new key keeps the old key's permissions.

Roll a key straight away if:

- it was committed to a code repository or shared in chat;
- someone who had it leaves your team;
- you see requests you don't recognise in the audit log.

To stop a key immediately, **revoke** it instead.

## When a key is refused

Errors from key checks include a `code` you can act on:

| Status | `code` | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `authorization_invalid` | The header isn't `Authorization: Bearer <secret key>`. |
| 401 | `public_key_not_allowed` | You sent a public key (`pk_`). Use your secret key. |
| 401 | `api_key_invalid` | The key doesn't exist, or a test key was used where a live key is needed. |
| 401 | `api_key_revoked` | The key was revoked. |
| 401 | `api_key_expired` | The key has expired. Create a new one. |
| 403 | `ip_not_allowed` | The request came from an IP address that isn't allowed. |
| 403 | `insufficient_scope` | The key is missing a permission. `required_scope` names it. |
| 403 | `route_not_permitted` | Restricted keys can't use this endpoint at all. |

```json
{
  "message": "This API key does not have the 'transfers:write' permission required for this request.",
  "code": "insufficient_scope",
  "required_scope": "transfers:write"
}
```

<Tip>
  Keys with an expiry date send an `X-Key-Expires-At` header on every response. Alert on it so a key never expires by surprise.
</Tip>

---

# Test mode and going live
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/test-mode

Every Modem Pay account has two separate worlds: **test** and **live**. You build and try everything in test mode. When it works, you switch your keys and go live. Your code doesn't change.

## What's different in test mode

| | Test mode | Live mode |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Keys | `sk_test_…`, `pk_test_…` | `sk_live_…`, `pk_live_…` |
| Money | Nothing real moves | Real payments and payouts |
| Data | Test payments, customers, links, sub-accounts, webhooks | Live ones, completely separate |
| Webhooks | Your test webhook URL | Your live webhook URL |
| Needs KYC | No | Yes |

The mode comes from the key. A test key only ever sees test data. A live key only ever sees live data. If you get a `404` for something you know exists, check you're using a key from the same mode.

Use the **Test mode** switch in the dashboard to see your test data.

## Try your integration

<Steps>
  <Step title="Take a test payment">
    Follow the [Quickstart](/documentation/quickstart), or from your terminal:

    ```bash
    npm install -g modem-pay-cli
    modempay login
    modempay transaction init --amount 100
    ```
  </Step>
  <Step title="Receive webhooks on your machine">
    ```bash
    modempay listen --forward-url http://localhost:3000/webhook
    ```
    Every test event is forwarded to your local server, signed exactly as in production. See [Modem Pay CLI](/documentation/cli).
  </Step>
  <Step title="Test the unhappy paths">
    Cancel a payment, close the checkout, send a webhook your server rejects. Your system should handle each one.

    ```bash
    modempay trigger charge.failed
    modempay trigger charge.cancelled
    ```
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Go-live checklist

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="1. Get verified (KYC)" icon="id-card">
    Submit your business documents in the dashboard. You can't take live payments until they're approved. The dashboard shows exactly which documents are still missing.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="2. Create live keys the safe way" icon="key">
    Create a **restricted** live key for each system, with only the permissions it needs. Add IP allowlists for your servers, and payout limits on any key that can send money. See [API keys](/documentation/authentication).
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="3. Store keys as secrets" icon="lock">
    Put live keys in environment variables or a secrets manager. Never in your code, your website or your mobile app.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="4. Add your live webhook" icon="bell">
    Add your live webhook URL in the dashboard and store its signing secret. Live and test webhooks have different secrets. Check that your endpoint [verifies signatures](/documentation/core/webhooks#verify-the-signature).
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="5. Mark orders paid from the webhook" icon="circle-check">
    Don't rely on the customer reaching your `return_url`. People close tabs. Fulfil orders when you receive `charge.succeeded`, or after [verifying the payment](/documentation/payment-intents/management) on your server.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="6. Use idempotency keys for payouts" icon="shield">
    Send a unique `Idempotency-Key` with every payout so a retry can never pay twice.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="7. Run one small real payment" icon="flag-checkered">
    Pay yourself 10 GMD on your live site and check the order, the webhook and your balance.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

<Note>
  Data never moves between modes. Payment links, customers, coupons, sub-accounts and webhooks you made in test mode need to be created again in live mode.
</Note>

---

# Errors
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/errors

When a request fails, Modem Pay returns an HTTP status of 400 or higher and a JSON body with a `message` you can show or log. Many errors also have a `code` your code can check.

```json
{
  "message": "This API key does not have the 'refunds:write' permission required for this request.",
  "code": "insufficient_scope",
  "required_scope": "refunds:write"
}
```

<Tip>
  Check `code` in your logic, not `message`. Messages are written for people and may change. Codes don't.
</Tip>

## Status codes

| Status | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | The request is missing something or has a wrong value. Validation errors list every problem in `message`, separated by commas. | Fix the request. Don't retry it unchanged. |
| `401` | No API key, or the key is wrong, revoked or expired. | Check the key. See [API keys](/documentation/authentication#when-a-key-is-refused). |
| `403` | The key works but isn't allowed to do this, or the IP address isn't allowed. | Add the permission or IP address, or use another key. |
| `404` | The thing you asked for doesn't exist, or belongs to another account or mode. | Check the ID, and that you're using a test key for test data and a live key for live data. |
| `409` | The request clashes with the current state, for example a duplicate. | Fetch the latest state before trying again. |
| `410` | The endpoint has been removed. | Move to the endpoint named in `message`. |
| `413` | The request body is too large. | Send less data per request. |
| `429` | Too many requests. | Wait, then retry. See [Rate limits](#rate-limits). |
| `500` | Something went wrong on our side. | Retry with backoff. If it keeps happening, email support. |
| `503` | A service we depend on is busy or unavailable. | Retry shortly. |

## Error codes you may see

| `code` | Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `authorization_invalid` | 401 | The `Authorization` header isn't `Bearer <secret key>`. |
| `api_key_missing` | 401 | The header has no key. |
| `public_key_not_allowed` | 401 | A public key was sent where a secret key is needed. |
| `api_key_invalid` | 401 | The key doesn't exist or doesn't match the mode. |
| `api_key_revoked` | 401 | The key was revoked. |
| `api_key_expired` | 401 | The key has expired. `expired_at` says when. |
| `ip_not_allowed` | 403 | The request came from an IP address that isn't on the allowlist. |
| `insufficient_scope` | 403 | The key is missing the permission in `required_scope`. |
| `route_not_permitted` | 403 | Restricted keys can't call this endpoint. |
| `per_transfer_limit_exceeded` | 403 | A payout is above the key's per-payout limit. |
| `daily_transfer_limit_exceeded` | 403 | The payout would take the key over its daily limit. |
| `RATE_LIMIT` | 429 | Too many payout requests in a short time. |
| `VELOCITY_LIMIT` | 429 | The account has sent too much value in the current window. |
| `CONCURRENCY_LIMIT` | 429 | Too many payouts are already being processed. |
| `ACCOUNT_THROTTLED` | 429 | Payouts are paused for a while after many rejected payouts. |
| `INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY` | 503 | Payout capacity is used up for now. Retry shortly. |
| `BATCH_TOO_LARGE` | 400 | A bulk payout has too many items. The limit is 1,000. |

## Rate limits

Requests to `/v1` are limited per business over a rolling 15-minute window. Payouts have their own, stricter limits to protect your balance.

When you hit a limit you get a `429`:

```json
{
  "message": "Too many requests from this account, please try again in 312 seconds.",
  "retryAfter": 312
}
```

Wait `retryAfter` seconds before trying again. Responses also carry the standard `RateLimit` headers, so you can slow down before you reach the limit.

Need a higher limit? Email [info@modempay.com](mailto:info@modempay.com) with your expected volume.

## Retries in the SDKs

The SDKs retry failed requests that are likely to be temporary, such as network errors and `5xx` responses. They try up to **3 times** by default, waiting a little longer each time.

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs
const modempay = new ModemPay(process.env.MODEMPAY_SECRET_KEY, {
  maxRetries: 3, // 0 turns retries off
});
```
```python python
modem_pay = ModemPay(api_key="sk_test_...", config={"maxRetries": 3})
```
</CodeGroup>

To hide the retry log lines but keep retrying, set `RETRY_LOGGING=false` in your environment.

<Warning>
  Before retrying a payout yourself, send the same `Idempotency-Key` header as the first attempt. Then a retry can never pay someone twice. See [Mobile money payouts](/documentation/payouts/mobile-money#send-a-payout).
</Warning>

## Timeouts

SDK requests time out after **60 seconds** by default. You can change this (in seconds):

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs
const modempay = new ModemPay(process.env.MODEMPAY_SECRET_KEY, {
  timeout: 20,
});
```
```python python
modem_pay = ModemPay(api_key="sk_test_...", config={"timeout": 20})
```
</CodeGroup>

If a payment or payout request times out, don't assume it failed. Look it up by ID or reference first, or wait for the webhook.

---

# Choose an integration
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/payments/overview

All five options use the same checkout, accept the same payment methods and send the same webhooks. They differ in how much you build.

| | Code needed | Customer pays on | Key used | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Payment links](/documentation/core/payment-links) | None | Modem Pay's page | — | Selling on WhatsApp, Instagram, by SMS |
| [Pay button](/documentation/payments/drop-in) | One HTML tag | A pop-up on your page | Public | Simple websites, donations |
| [HTML Checkout](/documentation/payments/html-checkout) | One HTML form | Modem Pay's page | Public | Static sites with no backend |
| [Checkout pop-up](/documentation/payments/modem-inline) | A few lines of JavaScript | A pop-up on your page | Public | Shops that want to react in the browser |
| [Your own checkout](/documentation/payments/custom) | Server code | Modem Pay's page or your own UI | Secret | Apps with a backend, split payments, saved customers |

<Tip>
  Not sure? Start with **payment intents** from your server ([Quickstart](/documentation/quickstart)). It works for any app, and you can add the pop-up or button later.
</Tip>

## Payment methods

Customers choose how to pay at checkout. Which methods appear depends on your account and country.

| Method | Type |
| --- | --- |
| Wave | Mobile wallet |
| Afrimoney | Mobile wallet |
| QMoney | Mobile wallet |
| APS | Mobile wallet |
| Yonna | Mobile wallet |
| Card | Bank card |
| USDT, USDC | [Stablecoins](/documentation/stablecoins/accept-payments) |

To list what's switched on for your account, call `GET /v1/payments/gateways`.

To limit the choice for one payment, set `payment_methods` when you create it, for example `["wallet"]` to hide cards. To skip checkout and charge one wallet directly, use [direct charge](/documentation/payment-intents/direct-charge).

## Every integration, the same rules

- **Minimum amount** is 10 GMD.
- **Confirm payments on your server.** Use the [webhook](/documentation/core/webhooks) or [verify the payment](/documentation/payment-intents/management). Never trust only a redirect or a browser callback.
- **Keep secret keys on your server.** Browser options use your public key.

---

# Payment links
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/core/payment-links

A payment link opens a Modem Pay checkout page for a product, a service or a donation. Send it on WhatsApp, put it in your Instagram bio, print it as a QR code or add it to an email. Every link can be used again and again until you turn it off.

<Tip>
  You don't need the API for this. Create links in the dashboard under **Payment links**. Use the API when you want to create links from your own system, for example one per product.
</Tip>

## What you can set

| Field | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | No | Shown at the top of the checkout page. |
| `description` | No | What the customer is paying for. |
| `amount` | No | A fixed price. **Leave it out** to let the customer type any amount, which is good for donations and tips. |
| `currency` | Yes | `GMD`. |
| `redirect_url` | No | Where the customer goes after paying. |
| `cancel_url` | No | Where the customer goes if they cancel. |
| `custom_fields` | No | Extra questions to ask at checkout, like `"Student ID"` or `"Delivery address"`. Answers come back in `custom_fields_values` on the transaction and webhook. |

## Create a link

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs
const link = await modempay.paymentLinks.create({
  title: "Wax print dress",
  description: "Size M, pick up at Kairaba Avenue",
  amount: 3500,
  currency: "GMD",
  redirect_url: "https://yourshop.gm/thanks",
  custom_fields: ["Pickup date"],
});

console.log(link.payment_link); // share this
```

```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://api.modempay.com/v1/payment-links \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Wax print dress",
    "description": "Size M, pick up at Kairaba Avenue",
    "amount": 3500,
    "currency": "GMD",
    "redirect_url": "https://yourshop.gm/thanks",
    "custom_fields": ["Pickup date"]
  }'
```
</CodeGroup>

The response includes the URL to share:

```json
{
  "id": "ed46f172-0c9e-4d53-862d-0afbb85d6f88",
  "type": "single-charge",
  "status": "active",
  "title": "Wax print dress",
  "amount": 3500,
  "currency": "GMD",
  "custom_fields": ["Pickup date"],
  "unique_code": "aa57aa1a28655934…",
  "payment_link": "https://test.checkout.modempay.com/pay/aa57aa1a28655934…",
  "test_mode": true,
  "createdAt": "2025-02-13T12:11:17.695Z"
}
```

## Manage links

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs
// Get one
const link = await modempay.paymentLinks.retrieve("ed46f172-…");

// Change it, or turn it off
await modempay.paymentLinks.update("ed46f172-…", { status: "inactive" });

// List all
const links = await modempay.paymentLinks.list();

// Delete
await modempay.paymentLinks.delete("ed46f172-…");
```
</CodeGroup>

You can update `title`, `description`, `amount`, `currency`, `redirect_url`, `cancel_url`, `custom_fields` and `status`. An `inactive` link can't be paid. Set it back to `active` to reopen it.

## Know when someone paid

Every payment through a link sends a `charge.succeeded` [webhook](/documentation/core/webhooks). The payload has `payment_link_id`, so you can tell which link was paid, and `custom_fields_values` with the customer's answers.

You can also see every payment for a link in the dashboard.

## Links, intents or invoices?

| Use | When |
| --- | --- |
| **Payment link** | The same price for many customers, shared by hand. |
| **[Payment intent](/documentation/payment-intents/create)** | One payment for one order, created by your server. |
| **[Invoice](/billing/invoices/introduction)** | A bill for one customer, with line items, a due date and reminders. |

---

# Pay button
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/payments/drop-in

A self-contained Web Component that opens the Modem Pay checkout modal when clicked. Works in plain HTML and any JavaScript framework, no dependencies, no build step.

## Installation

Add the script to your page. That's it, the `<modempay-button>` element is now available everywhere on the page.

```html html
<script src="https://api.modempay.com/js/modempay-button.js"></script>
```

## Quick Start

```html html
<script src="https://api.modempay.com/js/modempay-button.js"></script>

<modempay-button
  merchant="pk_live_xxxx"
  amount="500"
  currency="GMD"
  description="Order #1042"
/>
```

Clicking the button opens the Modem Pay checkout modal. The SDK and stylesheets are loaded automatically, no manual initialization needed.

## Attributes

| Attribute     | Required | Default                          | Description                                 |
| ------------- | -------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `merchant`    | Yes      | —                                | Your Modem Pay **public key**               |
| `amount`      | No       | —                                | Payment amount. Omit to show an input field |
| `currency`    | No       | `GMD`                            | ISO currency code                           |
| `description` | No       | —                                | Description shown in the checkout modal     |
| `label`       | No       | `Secure checkout with Modem Pay` | Override the button text                    |
| `color`       | No       | `#16a34a`                        | Primary button color                        |
| `radius`      | No       | `12`                             | Border radius in pixels                     |
| `disabled`    | No       | —                                | Disables the button when present            |

## Usage Examples

### Custom label

```html html
<modempay-button
  merchant="pk_live_xxxx"
  amount="1200"
  description="Concert Ticket"
  label="Buy Ticket"
/>
```

### Custom brand color

```html html
<modempay-button merchant="pk_live_xxxx" amount="500" color="#2563eb" />
```

### Dynamic amount (user enters amount)

Omit the `amount` attribute and the button renders an input field for the user to fill in. The minimum accepted amount is **10 GMD**.

```html html
<modempay-button merchant="pk_live_xxxx" description="Donation" />
```

## Usage in React

Web Components don't render through JSX, so use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` to mount the button. Load the script once (e.g. in `index.html` or a `useEffect`), then render the element like this:

```jsx jsx
export default function CheckoutButton() {
  return (
    <div
      dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{
        __html: `<modempay-button
          merchant="pk_test_xxxx"
          amount="10"
          currency="GMD"
          description="Order #1042"
        />`,
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

To listen for events in React, attach them via a `ref`:

```jsx jsx
import { useEffect, useRef } from "react";

export default function CheckoutButton() {
  const containerRef = useRef(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = containerRef.current?.querySelector("modempay-button");
    if (!el) return;

    const onSuccess = (e) => {
      console.log("Transaction:", e.detail.transaction);
    };

    el.addEventListener("modempay:success", onSuccess);
    return () => el.removeEventListener("modempay:success", onSuccess);
  }, []);

  return (
    <div
      ref={containerRef}
      dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{
        __html: `<modempay-button
          merchant="pk_test_xxxx"
          amount="10"
        />`,
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

<Note>
  Make sure the script is loaded before the component mounts. The easiest way is to add the `<script>` tag to your `public/index.html`.
</Note>

## Events

The button emits events at each stage of the payment lifecycle. Listen on the element directly.

### modempay:click

Fires when the button is clicked, **before** the checkout modal opens. The event is cancelable, call `event.preventDefault()` to stop the checkout from launching (e.g. to run validation first).

```javascript javascript
document
  .querySelector("modempay-button")
  .addEventListener("modempay:click", (event) => {
    // event.detail contains: merchant, amount, currency, description
    console.log(event.detail);

    // Optionally cancel checkout
    // event.preventDefault();
  });
```

### modempay:success

Fires when the payment completes. The completed transaction object is available at `event.detail.transaction`.

```javascript javascript
document
  .querySelector("modempay-button")
  .addEventListener("modempay:success", (event) => {
    const transaction = event.detail.transaction;

    console.log("Transaction ID:", transaction.id);
    console.log("Amount paid:", transaction.amount);
    console.log("Status:", transaction.status);
  });
```

### modempay:error

Fires if something goes wrong during the payment process. The error message is at `event.detail.message`.

```javascript javascript
document
  .querySelector("modempay-button")
  .addEventListener("modempay:error", (event) => {
    console.error("Payment failed:", event.detail.message);
  });
```

### modempay:cancel

Fires when the user closes the checkout modal without completing the payment. No detail payload.

```javascript javascript
document
  .querySelector("modempay-button")
  .addEventListener("modempay:cancel", () => {
    console.log("User closed the checkout modal.");
  });
```

## Styling

Customize the button with CSS custom properties. Set them on the element itself or in your stylesheet.

| Variable           | Description          | Default   |
| ------------------ | -------------------- | --------- |
| `--mp-color`       | Primary button color | `#16a34a` |
| `--mp-color-hover` | Hover state color    | `#15803d` |
| `--mp-radius`      | Border radius        | `12px`    |

```css
modempay-button {
  --mp-color: #2563eb;
  --mp-color-hover: #1d4ed8;
  --mp-radius: 16px;
}
```

## Accessibility

The button is built with accessibility in mind:

- Full keyboard navigation
- `aria-label` that includes the payment amount
- `aria-busy` set during loading so screen readers announce the state
- Visible focus ring on keyboard navigation
- Disabled state properly conveyed to assistive technology

## Accepted Payment Methods

Supported wallets are shown directly on the button to build user trust at the point of payment.

```
Wave · QMoney · AfriMoney · APS
```

## Browser Support

Works in all modern browsers that support the Web Components standard.

| Browser | Supported |
| ------- | --------- |
| Chrome  | ✅        |
| Edge    | ✅        |
| Firefox | ✅        |
| Safari  | ✅        |

Internet Explorer and browsers without `customElements` support are not supported.

# Checkout pop-up
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/payments/modem-inline

The pop-up lets customers pay without leaving your site. You open it with one function call and get told when the payment finishes or the customer closes it.

<Tip>
  Just need a button? The [pay button](/documentation/payments/drop-in) wraps this pop-up in a single HTML tag.
</Tip>

## Add it to your page

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://api.modempay.com/dist/main.css" />
<script src="https://api.modempay.com/js/v1.js"></script>

<button type="button" onclick="pay()">Pay now</button>

<script>
  function pay() {
    const modal = ModemPayCheckout({
      public_key: "pk_test_...",
      amount: 450,
      title: "Course payment",
      customer_email: "customer@example.com",
      metadata: { order_id: "1042" },
      callback: (transaction) => {
        // The payment finished. Confirm it on your server before delivering.
        fetch("/orders/1042/confirm", {
          method: "POST",
          headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
          body: JSON.stringify({ transaction_id: transaction.id }),
        });
        modal.close();
      },
      onClose: (cancelled) => {
        if (cancelled) console.log("Customer closed checkout without paying.");
      },
    });
  }
</script>
```

<Warning>
  This code runs in the browser, so it uses your **public** key. Never put your secret key here.
</Warning>

## Options

| Option | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `public_key` | Your public key. Required. | `"pk_test_…"` |
| `amount` | Amount to charge, in GMD. Required. | `450` |
| `currency` | Defaults to `GMD`. | `"GMD"` |
| `payment_methods` | Which kinds of method to offer. | `"wallet,card"` |
| `title` | Short title shown at checkout. | `"Course payment"` |
| `description` | Longer description. | `"Access to premium content"` |
| `customer` | An existing [customer](/documentation/core/customers) ID. Their saved payment methods are offered. | `"7e1908bb-…"` |
| `customer_name`, `customer_email`, `customer_phone` | Fill in checkout for the customer. | `"Awa Jallow"` |
| `metadata` | Your own data. Comes back on the transaction and webhook. | `{ "order_id": "1042" }` |
| `return_url` | Redirect here after payment, instead of calling `callback`. | `"https://yoursite.com/thanks"` |
| `cancel_url` | Redirect here on cancel, instead of calling `onClose`. | `"https://yoursite.com/cart"` |
| `callback` | Called with the transaction when the payment finishes. | `(transaction) => {}` |
| `onClose` | Called when the pop-up closes. `cancelled` is `true` if the customer didn't pay. | `(cancelled) => {}` |

## Redirects or callbacks?

- If you set `return_url`, the customer is redirected after paying and `callback` is **not** called.
- If you set `cancel_url`, the customer is redirected on cancel and `onClose` is **not** called.

Use the callbacks to stay on the page, like a single-page app. Use the URLs for a classic "thank you" page.

<Note>
  `callback` fires as soon as the payment finishes, while the pop-up may still be open. Close it with `modal.close()` when you're ready.
</Note>

## Confirm on your server

A browser callback can be faked. Before you deliver anything, check the payment on your server, either from the `charge.succeeded` [webhook](/documentation/core/webhooks) or by [looking it up](/documentation/core/transactions#get-a-transaction) with your secret key.

See a full example with a "verifying…" state: [CodePen](https://codepen.io/mercury-sms/embed/EaYNGOv?default-tab=html%2Cresult).

---

# HTML Checkout
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/payments/html-checkout

Put a form on your page. When the customer clicks the button, they go to Modem Pay's checkout, pay, and come back to your site.

```html
<form action="https://test.checkout.modempay.com/api/pay" method="POST">
  <input type="hidden" name="public_key" value="pk_test_...">
  <input type="hidden" name="amount" value="150">
  <input type="hidden" name="currency" value="GMD">
  <input type="hidden" name="return_url" value="https://yoursite.com/thanks">
  <input type="hidden" name="cancel_url" value="https://yoursite.com/cart">
  <button type="submit">Pay GMD 150</button>
</form>
```

Try it:

<iframe
  height="400"
  width="100%"
  title="Modem Pay HTML Checkout"
  src="https://codepen.io/mercury-sms/embed/VYZmLQZ?default-tab=result"
  frameborder="0"
  allow="clipboard-write; fullscreen"
  referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
  allowfullscreen
></iframe>

## Form fields

| Field | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `public_key` | Yes | Your **public** key (`pk_test_…` or `pk_live_…`). Never your secret key. |
| `amount` | Yes | Amount in GMD, at least 10. |
| `currency` | No | `GMD`. |
| `return_url` | Recommended | Where the customer goes after paying. |
| `cancel_url` | Recommended | Where the customer goes if they cancel. |
| `customer_name` | No | Fills in checkout for the customer. |
| `customer_email` | No | Fills in checkout for the customer. |
| `customer_phone` | No | Fills in checkout for the customer. |
| `metadata` | No | Your own data, like an order ID. It comes back on the transaction and webhook. |

## Confirm the payment

Anyone can edit a form in their browser, including the amount. So **before you deliver anything, check the payment on your server**:

- receive the `charge.succeeded` [webhook](/documentation/core/webhooks) and check its `amount`, or
- look the payment up with your secret key.

<Tip>
  Want customers to pay without leaving your page? Use the [pay button](/documentation/payments/drop-in) or the [checkout pop-up](/documentation/payments/modem-inline) instead. Both are just as easy.
</Tip>

---

# Your own checkout
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/payments/custom

This is the most flexible way to accept payments. Your server creates a **payment intent** for each order, so the price can't be changed in the browser, and you can add split payments, coupons, saved customers and your own references.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Customer
    participant S as Your server
    participant M as Modem Pay
    C->>S: Clicks "Checkout"
    S->>M: Create payment intent
    M-->>S: payment_link
    S-->>C: Redirect to payment_link
    C->>M: Pays
    M-->>C: Back to your return_url
    M->>S: Webhook: charge.succeeded
    S->>S: Mark order paid
```

## Complete example

A small Express app: a checkout button, a page to come back to, and a webhook endpoint.

<CodeGroup>
```javascript server.js
import express from "express";
import ModemPay from "modem-pay";

const modempay = new ModemPay(process.env.MODEMPAY_SECRET_KEY);
const app = express();
const DOMAIN = "http://localhost:7024";

// 1. Create the payment on the server, with the price from your database.
app.post("/checkout", express.urlencoded({ extended: false }), async (req, res) => {
  const order = { id: "1042", amount: 2000, title: "Stubborn Attachments" };

  const intent = await modempay.paymentIntents.create({
    amount: order.amount,
    title: order.title,
    metadata: { order_id: order.id },
    return_url: `${DOMAIN}/success.html`,
    cancel_url: `${DOMAIN}/cancel.html`,
  });

  // 2. Send the customer to pay.
  res.redirect(303, intent.data.payment_link);
});

// 3. Mark the order paid when Modem Pay tells you. Use the raw body to check the signature.
app.post("/webhook", express.raw({ type: "application/json" }), (req, res) => {
  let event;
  try {
    event = modempay.webhooks.composeEventDetails(
      req.body.toString("utf8"),
      req.headers["x-modem-signature"],
      process.env.MODEMPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET,
    );
  } catch {
    return res.status(400).send("Invalid signature");
  }

  res.sendStatus(200);

  if (event.event === "charge.succeeded") {
    const orderId = event.payload.metadata?.order_id;
    // markOrderPaid(orderId, event.payload.amount)
  }
});

app.use(express.static("public"));
app.listen(7024, () => console.log("Running on http://localhost:7024"));
```

```html public/index.html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <body>
    <h3>Stubborn Attachments</h3>
    <p>GMD 2,000.00</p>
    <form action="/checkout" method="POST">
      <button type="submit">Checkout</button>
    </form>
  </body>
</html>
```

```html public/success.html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <body>
    <p>Thanks! We're confirming your payment and will email you shortly.</p>
  </body>
</html>
```

```html public/cancel.html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <body>
    <p>Payment cancelled. Your cart is still waiting for you.</p>
  </body>
</html>
```
</CodeGroup>

Run it with your test key and webhook secret, then use the [CLI](/documentation/cli) to get webhooks on your machine:

```bash
modempay listen --forward-url http://localhost:7024/webhook
```

## Why the price comes from the server

The browser only sends "I want to check out". Your server decides the amount. Nobody can change the price by editing your page.

    Give money back, in full or in part.

# Payment intents
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/payment-intents/overview

A **payment intent** says "this customer should pay this amount". You create it on your server, Modem Pay gives you a `payment_link`, and the customer pays there. Every integration, from the pay button to payment links, creates one behind the scenes.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[requires_payment_method] --> B[processing]
    B --> C[successful]
    B --> D[failed]
    A --> E[cancelled]
    A --> F[expired]
    F -- restored --> A
```

## What you can send

Only `amount` is required.

| Field | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `amount` | How much to charge, in GMD. At least 10. |
| `currency` | Defaults to your account's currency. |
| `title`, `description` | Shown to the customer at checkout. |
| `customer` | A [customer](/documentation/core/customers) ID. Their saved payment methods are offered. |
| `customer_name`, `customer_email`, `customer_phone` | Fill in checkout for a customer you haven't saved. |
| `payment_methods` | Limit the choice, like `["wallet"]` or `["card"]`. |
| `payment_method` | Charge one specific saved payment method. |
| `network`, `account_number` | [Direct charge](/documentation/payment-intents/direct-charge) a mobile wallet. |
| `coupon` | A [coupon](/documentation/core/coupons) ID or name. Its discount is taken off. |
| `sub_account`, `sub_account_group` | [Split the payment](/documentation/split-payments/initialize-payment) with partners. |
| `metadata` | Your own data, like an order ID. Comes back on the transaction and every webhook. |
| `return_url` | Where the customer goes after paying. |
| `cancel_url` | Where the customer goes if they cancel. |
| `callback_url` | Send this payment's events here instead of your webhook. See [Callback URL](/documentation/payment-intents/callback_url). |
| `skip_url_validation` | Set `true` when `return_url` or `cancel_url` is a mobile app deep link, like `myapp://paid`. |

## What you get back

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Payment intent created successfully. Please proceed to complete the payment.",
  "data": {
    "intent_secret": "bfa7eb3ea516ee15f80915a922c00242…",
    "payment_link": "https://test.checkout.modempay.com/…",
    "amount": 450,
    "currency": "GMD",
    "status": "requires_payment_method",
    "expires_at": "2025-03-01T12:30:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `payment_link` | Send the customer here to pay. |
| `intent_secret` | Use it to [look the intent up](/documentation/payment-intents/management#check-a-payment) later. Keep it on your server. |
| `expires_at` | After this, the link stops working and you get `payment_intent.expired`. |
| `status` | Where the payment stands. See below. |

## Statuses

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `requires_payment_method` | Waiting for the customer to pay. |
| `processing` | The customer is paying right now. |
| `successful` | Paid. |
| `failed` | The payment didn't go through. |
| `cancelled` | You or the customer cancelled it. |
| `expired` | It wasn't paid in time. |

## Next

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Create a payment intent" icon="plus" href="/documentation/payment-intents/create">
    Examples from simple to saved customers.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Check, list and cancel" icon="magnifying-glass" href="/documentation/payment-intents/management">
    Confirm a payment and clean up old ones.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

# Create a payment intent
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/payment-intents/create

You only need an `amount`. Add more details to fill in checkout for the customer, limit how they pay, or charge a method they saved before. Every option is listed in [Payment intents](/documentation/payment-intents/overview#what-you-can-send).

<iframe
  width="100%"
  height="425"
  src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/Gox1JSWZYdg?si=YoJPOWZHxGNiaRUt"
  title="YouTube video player"
  frameborder="0"
  allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share"
  referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
  allowfullscreen
></iframe>


## Just the amount

The simplest case: all you need is the amount to charge. This is the most basic
setup.

- **Situation**: You want a customer to pay GMD 450, and you're not adding a customer record or any other optional details.
- **Request**:

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs 
const paymentIntent = await modempay.paymentIntents.create({ amount: 450 });
```
```python python 
payment_intent = modem_pay.payment_intents.create(params={"amount": 450})
```
```php php 
$payment_intent = $modemPay->paymentIntents()->create(['amount' => 450]);
```
```bash cURL 
cURL -X POST "https://api.modempay.com/v1/payments" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "amount": 450,
      "from_sdk": false
    }
  }'
```
</CodeGroup>

- **Result**: A Payment Intent is created, along with a link to the payment page where the customer pays.

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Payment intent created successfully. Please proceed to complete the payment.",
  "data": {
    "intent_secret": "8816a8e679d9df252fa80d09ebe21efaa3a8980cb053cb64afeed44c5df696f4",
    "payment_link": "https://test.checkout.modempay.com/6b63ccef-0232-4be1-b53d-be6823767874",
    "amount": 450,
    "currency": "GMD",
    "expires_at": "2025-02-13T12:31:15.601Z",
    "status": "requires_payment_method"
  }
}
```

## Amount and customer

Here you add the customer who's paying, on top of the amount. This ties the
payment to a specific customer so it's easier to keep track of.

- **Situation**: You want to charge GMD 450 and link it to a particular customer.
- **Request**:

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs 
const paymentIntent = await modempay.paymentIntents.create({
    amount: 450,
    customer: "d9bf8831-4db5-4a1c-8aa0-3de72492f330",
});
```
```python python 
payment_intent = modem_pay.payment_intents.create(
    params={"amount": 450, "customer": "d9bf8831-4db5-4a1c-8aa0-3de72492f330"}
)
```
```php php 
$payment_intent = $modemPay->paymentIntents()->create([
    'amount' => 450,
    'customer' => 'd9bf8831-4db5-4a1c-8aa0-3de72492f330',
]);
```
```bash cURL 
cURL -X POST "https://api.modempay.com/v1/payments" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "amount": 450,
      "customer": "d9bf8831-4db5-4a1c-8aa0-3de72492f330",
      "from_sdk": false
    }
  }'
```
</CodeGroup>

## Amount, customer, and payment methods

A more specific setup: you set the amount, link a customer, and decide ahead of
time which payment methods the customer can use. Handy when you want to limit
things to certain methods.

- **Situation**: You want to charge GMD 450, link it to a customer, and only allow a particular payment method.
- **Request**:

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs 
const paymentIntent = await modempay.paymentIntents.create({
    amount: 450,
    customer: "d9bf8831-4db5-4a1c-8aa0-3de72492f330",
    payment_methods: ["card"],
});
```
```python python 
payment_intent = modem_pay.payment_intents.create(
    params={
        "amount": 450,
        "customer": "d9bf8831-4db5-4a1c-8aa0-3de72492f330",
        "payment_methods": ["card"],
    }
)
```
```php php 
$payment_intent = $modemPay->paymentIntents()->create([
    'amount' => 450,
    'customer' => 'd9bf8831-4db5-4a1c-8aa0-3de72492f330',
    'payment_methods' => ['card'],
]);
```
```bash cURL 
cURL -X POST "https://api.modempay.com/v1/payments" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "amount": 450,
      "customer": "d9bf8831-4db5-4a1c-8aa0-3de72492f330",
      "payment_methods": ["card"],
      "from_sdk": false
    }
  }'
```
</CodeGroup>

## Amount, customer, and a specific saved payment method

Here you point to one of the customer's saved payment methods by its ID. Useful
when you want to charge a saved card or bank account directly.

- **Situation**: You want to charge GMD 450, link it to a customer, and use a specific saved payment method from their account. This lets you charge a saved method straight away, which makes things quicker for returning customers.

- **Request**:

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs 
const paymentIntent = await modempay.paymentIntents.create({
    amount: 450,
    payment_method: "ad47ccb9-687c-475b-90dc-1dd3b4cba68e",
    customer: "d9bf8831-4db5-4a1c-8aa0-3de72492f330",
});
```
```python python 
payment_intent = modem_pay.payment_intents.create(
    params={
        "amount": 450,
        "payment_method": "ad47ccb9-687c-475b-90dc-1dd3b4cba68e",
        "customer": "d9bf8831-4db5-4a1c-8aa0-3de72492f330",
    }
)
```
```php php 
$payment_intent = $modemPay->paymentIntents()->create([
    'amount' => 450,
    'payment_method' => 'ad47ccb9-687c-475b-90dc-1dd3b4cba68e',
    'customer' => 'd9bf8831-4db5-4a1c-8aa0-3de72492f330',
]);
```
```bash cURL 
cURL -X POST "https://api.modempay.com/v1/payments" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "amount": 450,
      "customer": "d9bf8831-4db5-4a1c-8aa0-3de72492f330",
      "payment_method": "ad47ccb9-687c-475b-90dc-1dd3b4cba68e",
      "from_sdk": false
    }
  }'
```
</CodeGroup>


## Next

Send the customer to `data.payment_link`, then confirm the payment with a [webhook](/documentation/core/webhooks) or by [checking it](/documentation/payment-intents/management#check-a-payment).

---

# Direct charge
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/payment-intents/direct-charge

If you already know the customer's wallet, send the `network` and `account_number` when you create the payment intent. The checkout opens with their wallet already filled in, so they only need to confirm.

This is great for apps where the customer has already given you their number, like a top-up or a delivery app.

| Network | `network` value |
| --- | --- |
| Wave | `wave` |
| Afrimoney | `afrimoney` |
| QMoney | `qmoney` |
| APS | `aps` |

The `account_number` is the 7-digit phone number, **without** the country code.

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs
const intent = await modempay.paymentIntents.create({
  amount: 450,
  network: "wave",
  account_number: "7000001",
});
```

```python python
intent = modem_pay.payment_intents.create(
    params={"amount": 450, "network": "wave", "account_number": "7000001"}
)
```

```php php
$intent = $modemPay->paymentIntents()->create([
    'amount' => 450,
    'network' => 'wave',
    'account_number' => '7000001',
]);
```

```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://api.modempay.com/v1/payments \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "data": { "amount": 450, "network": "wave", "account_number": "7000001" } }'
```
</CodeGroup>

Direct charge works with mobile money only. For cards, send the customer to the `payment_link` as usual.

The customer must still approve the payment. Confirm the result with the `charge.succeeded` [webhook](/documentation/core/webhooks), as with any other payment.

---

# Check, list and cancel
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/payment-intents/management

## Check a payment

Look a payment intent up by its `intent_secret`, which you got when you created it. Do this on your server before you deliver an order, if you're not using webhooks.

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs
const intent = await modempay.paymentIntents.retrieve("bfa7eb3ea516ee15f80915a922c00242…");

if (intent.status === "successful") {
  // deliver the order
}
```
```python python
intent = modem_pay.payment_intents.retrieve("bfa7eb3ea516ee15f80915a922c00242…")
```
```php php
$intent = $modemPay->paymentIntents()->retrieve("bfa7eb3ea516ee15f80915a922c00242…");
```
```bash cURL
curl "https://api.modempay.com/v1/payments/verify?intent_secret=bfa7eb3ea516ee15f80915a922c00242…" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```
</CodeGroup>

You get the payment intent back, with its `status`, `amount`, `currency`, `metadata`, `link` and customer.

<Tip>
  Check `amount` as well as `status`. That way you know the customer paid the right amount for the right order.
</Tip>

## List payment intents

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs
const intents = await modempay.paymentIntents.list({ limit: 10 });
```
```python python
intents = modem_pay.payment_intents.list(options={"limit": 10})
```
```php php
$intents = $modemPay->paymentIntents()->list(['limit' => 10]);
```
```bash cURL
curl "https://api.modempay.com/v1/payments?offset=0&limit=10" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```
</CodeGroup>

```json
{
  "data": [ ... ],
  "meta": { "total": 31 }
}
```

Use `limit` and `offset` to page through. `meta.total` is how many there are in all.

## Cancel a payment intent

Cancel an intent that should no longer be paid, for example when the customer empties their cart or the item sells out. A cancelled intent can't be paid.

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs
await modempay.paymentIntents.cancel("49ac6595-beba-480f-bc3d-33e5d4162c4c");
```
```python python
modem_pay.payment_intents.cancel("49ac6595-beba-480f-bc3d-33e5d4162c4c")
```
```php php
$modemPay->paymentIntents()->cancel("49ac6595-beba-480f-bc3d-33e5d4162c4c");
```
```bash cURL
curl -X PATCH https://api.modempay.com/v1/payments/49ac6595-beba-480f-bc3d-33e5d4162c4c \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```
</CodeGroup>

The intent's status becomes `cancelled` and you get a `payment_intent.cancelled` webhook.

---

# Callback URL
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/payment-intents/callback_url

Set `callback_url` when you create a payment intent, and that payment's events (`charge.succeeded`, `charge.failed` and the rest) go to that URL **instead of** your account [webhook](/documentation/core/webhooks).

This is useful when one Modem Pay account serves several systems, like a marketplace where each shop has its own server.

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs
const intent = await modempay.paymentIntents.create({
  amount: 450,
  callback_url: "https://shop-42.example.com/modempay",
});
```
```python python
intent = modem_pay.payment_intents.create(params={
    "amount": 450,
    "callback_url": "https://shop-42.example.com/modempay",
})
```
```php php
$intent = $modemPay->paymentIntents()->create([
    'amount' => 450,
    'callback_url' => 'https://shop-42.example.com/modempay',
]);
```
```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://api.modempay.com/v1/payments \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "data": { "amount": 450, "callback_url": "https://shop-42.example.com/modempay" } }'
```
</CodeGroup>

The body is the same as a webhook: `{ "event": "...", "payload": { ... } }`. Retries work the same way too: up to 3 more tries, 10 minutes apart.

## Verify a callback

Callbacks are signed differently from webhooks. There's no webhook secret here. Instead, the signing key is the **SHA-256 hash of your secret API key**, as lowercase hex.

| Header | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `x-modem-signature` | HMAC-SHA512 of the raw body, made with `sha256(secret_key)`. |
| `x-modem-signature-key` | The last 4 characters of the secret key that signed it. |

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs
import crypto from "crypto";

const signingKey = crypto
  .createHash("sha256")
  .update(process.env.MODEMPAY_SECRET_KEY)
  .digest("hex");

// rawBody: the request body exactly as received
const event = modempay.webhooks.composeEventDetails(
  rawBody,
  req.headers["x-modem-signature"],
  signingKey,
);
```
```python python
import hashlib, hmac, os

signing_key = hashlib.sha256(os.environ["MODEMPAY_SECRET_KEY"].encode()).hexdigest()
expected = hmac.new(signing_key.encode(), raw_body, hashlib.sha512).hexdigest()
valid = hmac.compare_digest(expected, request.headers.get("x-modem-signature", ""))
```
```php php
$signingKey = hash('sha256', getenv('MODEMPAY_SECRET_KEY'));

$event = $modemPay->webhooks()->composeEventDetails(
    file_get_contents('php://input'),
    $_SERVER['HTTP_X_MODEM_SIGNATURE'] ?? '',
    $signingKey
);
```
</CodeGroup>

<Note>
  Callbacks are signed with your **newest active** secret key on that account. After you [roll a key](/documentation/authentication#roll-a-key), callbacks are signed with the new one. If you keep several keys, use `x-modem-signature-key` to pick the right one.
</Note>

Use an HTTPS URL. As with webhooks, use the raw request body, and reply `200` quickly.

---

# Refunds
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/payment-intents/refund

You can refund a completed payment within **48 hours**. The money comes from your [payout balance](/documentation/core/balances) and goes back to the customer.

## Rules

- The transaction must be `completed`, or `partially_refunded` if you've already refunded part of it.
- The original payment must be no more than **48 hours** old.
- You can refund part of a payment, and refund again later, until the total refunded reaches the original amount.
- A processing charge may apply.

## Refund a payment

Identify the payment by its transaction `id`, `reference` or `transaction_reference`. Leave out `amount` for a full refund.

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs
// Full refund
await modempay.transactions.reverse("VOAO1CFEN7");

// Partial refund of 450 GMD
await modempay.transactions.reverse("VOAO1CFEN7", 450);
```

```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://api.modempay.com/v1/transactions/refund \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "reference": "VOAO1CFEN7", "amount": 450 }'
```
</CodeGroup>

A restricted key needs the `refunds:write` permission. Because refunds move money, give it only to systems that really need it.

## After a refund

- The transaction's status becomes `refunded`, or `partially_refunded` for a partial refund.
- You get a `charge.refunded` [webhook](/documentation/core/webhooks).
- The customer usually sees the money quickly, but their provider decides the exact timing. Let them know a refund is on its way.

<Tip>
  Need to give money back after 48 hours, or to a different number? Send a [payout](/documentation/payouts/mobile-money) instead.
</Tip>

---

# Customers
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/core/customers

A customer holds a name, email and phone number. Pass a customer's `id` when you create a payment intent and checkout is filled in for them. If they chose to save a payment method before, it's offered too.


## Create a customer

To create a customer, use the `modempay.customers.create()` method, which allows you to add key information like the customer's name, email, phone number, and an optional starting balance. The `distinct` option, when set to `true`, checks for existing customers with matching fields (e.g., email) to avoid duplicate entries. If `distinct` is omitted or set to `false`, a new customer entry will be created without duplicate checks.

**Sample Request:**

<CodeGroup>
```typescript nodejs
const customer = await modempay.customers.create(
    { name: "Zypheron Kade", email: "zypheron.kade42@protonmail.com", phone: "7000001" },
    { distinct: true }
);
```
```python python
customer = modem_pay.customers.create(
    params={
        "name": "Zypheron Kade",
        "email": "zypheron.kade42@protonmail.com",
        "phone": "7000001",
    },
    options={"distinct": True},
)
```
```bash cURL
cURL -X POST "https://api.modempay.com/v1/customers" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Zypheron Kade",
    "email": "zypheron.kade42@protonmail.com",
    "phone": "7000001",
    "config": { "distinct": true }
  }'
```
</CodeGroup>

**Sample Response:**

```json
{
  "id": "8a8c8a0e-c5d2-4692-a94b-25284d36adc7",
  "balance": 0,
  "name": "Zypheron Kade",
  "email": "zypheron.kade42@protonmail.com",
  "phone": "7000001",
  "business_id": "a10a51ae-05c8-406e-968c-7b1d309a77e0",
  "account_id": "7788dd90-3801-47a6-8597-b46eaa0a7d7d",
  "test_mode": true,
  "updatedAt": "2024-11-11T13:54:10.104Z",
  "createdAt": "2024-11-11T13:54:10.104Z"
}
```

---

## Retrieve a customer

To fetch a customer’s details, use `modempay.customers.retrieve(customerId)`. Replace `customerId` with the customer’s unique ID.

**Sample Request:**

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs 
const customer = await modempay.customers.retrieve(
  "8a8c8a0e-c5d2-4692-a94b-25284d36adc7"
);
```
```python python 
customer = modem_pay.customers.retrieve("8a8c8a0e-c5d2-4692-a94b-25284d36adc7")
```
```bash cURL 
cURL -X GET "https://api.modempay.com/v1/customers/8a8c8a0e-c5d2-4692-a94b-25284d36adc7" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>"
```
</CodeGroup>

**Sample Response:**

```json
{
  "id": "8a8c8a0e-c5d2-4692-a94b-25284d36adc7",
  "name": "Zypheron Kade",
  "email": "zypheron.kade42@protonmail.com",
  "phone": "7000001",
  "balance": 0,
  "business_id": "a10a51ae-05c8-406e-968c-7b1d309a77e0",
  "account_id": "7788dd90-3801-47a6-8597-b46eaa0a7d7d",
  "test_mode": true,
  "createdAt": "2024-11-11T13:54:10.104Z",
  "updatedAt": "2024-11-11T13:54:10.104Z"
}
```

---

## Update a customer

Update a customer's information using `modempay.customers.update(customerId, params)`. Specify the customer ID and the fields to update.

**Sample Request:**

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs 
const customer = await modempay.customers.update(
    "8a8c8a0e-c5d2-4692-a94b-25284d36adc7",
    { name: "Chibuike Okpara" }
);
```
```python python 
customer = modem_pay.customers.update(
    id="8a8c8a0e-c5d2-4692-a94b-25284d36adc7", params={"name": "Chibuike Okpara"}
)
```
```bash cURL 
cURL -X PUT "https://api.modempay.com/v1/customers/<customer_id>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "<parameter_1>": "<value_1>",
      "<parameter_2>": "<value_2>"
    }
  }'
```
</CodeGroup>

**Sample Response:**

```json
{
  "id": "8a8c8a0e-c5d2-4692-a94b-25284d36adc7",
  "name": "Chibuike Okpara",
  "email": "zypheron.kade42@protonmail.com",
```

## Delete a customer

Remove a customer from your records using `modempay.customers.delete(customerId)`. This action is irreversible.

**Sample Request:**

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs

```
```python python 
modem_pay.customers.delete("8a8c8a0e-c5d2-4692-a94b-25284d36adc7")
```
```bash cURL 
cURL -X DELETE "https://api.modempay.com/v1/customers/<customer_id>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>"
```
</CodeGroup>

# Mandates
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/core/mandates

When a customer ticks **save this payment method** at checkout, Modem Pay records a **mandate**: their permission to charge that method again. You can't create mandates yourself. Only the customer can, which protects you if a payment is ever disputed.

Mandates are what let you:

- offer a customer's saved wallet at checkout next time, and
- [charge a saved payment method](/documentation/payment-intents/create) for repeat payments.


## Get a mandate

Mandates are tied directly to specific payment methods and can only be retrieved by the associated payment method ID, allowing merchants to verify authorization.

**Parameters:**
- `payment_method` *(string)*: The unique identifier for the saved payment method linked to the mandate.

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs
const mandate = await modempay.mandates.retrieve(
    "ad47ccb9-687c-475b-90dc-1dd3b4cba68e"
);
```
</CodeGroup>

**Response:**

```json 
{
  "id": "5a7843ba-1fd5-4d2b-ab81-5db00ae84f96",
  "customer_acceptance": {
    "type": "charge",
    "accepted_at": 1731151351177
  },
  "payment_method": "ad47ccb9-687c-475b-90dc-1dd3b4cba68e",
  "payment_method_details": {
    "logo": "https://api.modempay.com/images/qcell.png",
    "type": "mobilepay",
    "group": "wallet-gm",
    "last4": "9944",
    "gateway": "qmoney",
    "fingerprint": "8d84c1b8ba568bce9b2590bfec618a65",
    "gateway_name": "QMoney"
  },
  "status": "active",
  "type": "one-time",
  "business_id": "a10a51ae-05c8-406e-968c-7b1d309a77e0",
  "account_id": "7788dd90-3801-47a6-8597-b46eaa0a7d7d",
  "test_mode": true,
  "createdAt": "2024-11-09T11:22:31.179Z",
  "updatedAt": "2024-11-09T12:00:01.527Z"
}
```

A restricted key needs the `payment_methods:read` permission.

# Coupons
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/core/coupons

Create a coupon once, then pass its `id` or `name` as `coupon` when you create a payment intent. Modem Pay checks the coupon's rules and takes the discount off the amount.

## Create a coupon

Use `modempay.coupons.create()` to create a coupon. Coupons can offer a fixed amount or percentage discount and support options like duration, redemption limits, and restrictions.

**Example: Creating a 15% Off Coupon for a Market Promotion**

<CodeGroup>
```typescript nodejs
async function createCoupon() {
  try {
    const coupon = await modempay.coupons.create({
      name: 'Market Fest 15% Off',
      percent_off: 15,
      duration: 'once',
      redeem_by: new Date('2025-06-30'),
      currency: 'GMD',
      restrictions: {
        first_time_transaction: false,
        minimum_amount: 100,
        minimum_amount_currency: 'GMD'
      }
    });
    console.log('Coupon created:', coupon);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error creating coupon:', error);
  }
}
```
</CodeGroup>

This creates a coupon offering 15% off for purchases of at least 100 GMD, valid until June 30, 2025, and redeemable once.

**Example: Creating a 50 GMD Off Coupon for Mobile Data**

<CodeGroup>
```typescript nodejs
async function createDataCoupon() {
  try {
    const coupon = await modempay.coupons.create({
      name: 'MobileDataDiscount',
      amount_off: 50, 
      duration: 'forever',
      currency: 'GMD',
      restrictions: {
        first_time_transaction: true,
        minimum_amount: 200, 
        minimum_amount_currency: 'GMD'
      },
    });
    console.log('Coupon created:', coupon);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error creating coupon:', error);
  }
}
```
</CodeGroup>

This coupon gives 50 GMD off for first-time data bundle purchases of 200 GMD or more, with no expiry or redemption limit.

**Key Parameters**

- `name` : Descriptive name (e.g., "MarketFest").
- `percent_off` : Percentage discount (e.g., 15 for 15%). Use amount_off for fixed amounts.
- `currency` : Set to "GMD" for all amounts.
- `duration` : "once", "repeating", or "forever".
- `duration_in_months` : Required if duration is "repeating".
- `max_redemptions` : Maximum uses of the coupon.
- `redeem_by` : Expiry date.
- `restrictions` : Conditions like minimum_amount or first_time_transaction.

## Get a coupon

Fetch a specific coupon’s details using `modempay.coupons.retrieve()`.

<CodeGroup>
```typescript nodejs
async function getCoupon(couponId) {
  try {
    const coupon = await modempay.coupons.retrieve(couponId);
    console.log('Coupon details:', coupon);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error retrieving coupon:', error);
  }
}
```
</CodeGroup>

## List coupons

View all coupons with `modempay.coupons.list()`, with options to paginate or filter.

<CodeGroup>
```typescript nodejs
async function listCoupons() {
  try {
    const coupons = await modempay.coupons.list({ limit: 5, search: 'Fest' });
    console.log('Coupons:', coupons);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error listing coupons:', error);
  }
}
```
</CodeGroup>

This retrieves up to 5 coupons with "Fest" in their name.

## Update a coupon

Modify a coupon’s properties (e.g., name, redemption limits) using `modempay.coupons.update()`.

<CodeGroup>
```typescript nodejs
async function updateCoupon(couponId) {
  try {
    const updatedCoupon = await modempay.coupons.update(couponId, {
      name: 'Extended Market Fest',
      max_redemptions: 75,
      redeem_by: new Date('2025-07-31')
    });
    console.log('Updated coupon:', updatedCoupon);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error updating coupon:', error);
  }
}
```
</CodeGroup>

This extends the coupon’s validity to July 31, 2025, and increases the redemption limit to 75.

## Delete a coupon

Permanently remove a coupon with `modempay.coupons.delete()`.

<CodeGroup>
```typescript nodejs
async function deleteCoupon(couponId) {
  try {
    await modempay.coupons.delete(couponId);
    console.log('Coupon deleted successfully');
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error deleting coupon:', error);
  }
}
```
</CodeGroup>

## Use a coupon on a payment

Apply a coupon to a [PaymentIntent](/documentation/payment-intents/overview) to discount the transaction. Include the coupon `id` or `name` in the `coupon` field when creating a [PaymentIntent](/documentation/payment-intents/overview).

<CodeGroup>
```typescript nodejs
async function createPaymentIntentWithCoupon(couponIdOrName) {
  try {
    const paymentIntent = await modempay.paymentIntents.create({
      amount: 150,
      currency: 'GMD',
      customer: '8a8c8a0e-c5d2-4692-a94b-25284d36adc7',
      coupon: couponIdOrName
    });
    console.log('Payment Intent with coupon:', paymentIntent);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error creating Payment Intent:', error);
  }
}
```
</CodeGroup>
