If the coupon offers 15% off and the original amount is 150 GMD, the discounted amount will be 127.50 GMD (assuming the coupon is valid and meets restrictions).

**How It Works**

- Modem Pay validates the coupon’s restrictions (e.g., `minimum_amount`, `first_time_transaction`).
- If valid, the discount (`percent_off` or `amount_off`) is applied to the `PaymentIntent`’s amount.
- The coupon’s `times_redeemed` increments upon successful application.

## Tips

- **Validate Restrictions**: Ensure the coupon’s `minimum_amount` aligns with your pricing.
- **Test Thoroughly**: Use test API keys to simulate coupon scenarios.
- **Monitor Usage**: Track active coupons and redemptions with `modempay.coupons.list()`.

## When a coupon doesn't apply

- **Invalid Coupon**: Verify the coupon ID and ensure `valid: true`.
- **Restrictions Not Met**: Check if the `PaymentIntent` meets `minimum_amount` or `first_time_transaction` requirements.
- **API Errors**: Confirm API key setup and network connectivity.

---

# Payouts
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/payouts/overview

Payouts (called **transfers** in the API) send money from your [payout balance](/documentation/core/balances) to a mobile money wallet. Use them for withdrawals, paying suppliers, salaries, winnings and refunds.

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Send one payout" icon="paper-plane" href="/documentation/payouts/mobile-money">
    Pay one Wave or Afrimoney wallet.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Send many at once" icon="users" href="/documentation/payouts/bulk-payout">
    Up to 1,000 payouts in one request.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Check the fee first" icon="calculator" href="/documentation/payouts/fees">
    Know the exact cost before you send.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Reverse a payout" icon="arrow-rotate-left" href="/documentation/payouts/reversals">
    Pull back a Wave payout sent to the wrong person.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## How a payout works

<Steps>
  <Step title="You send the request">
    With the amount, network, wallet number, the person's name and a unique `Idempotency-Key`.
  </Step>
  <Step title="We check it">
    Your balance must cover the amount plus the fee. We also run fraud and limit checks.
  </Step>
  <Step title="We send the money">
    The amount and fee leave your payout balance and the money goes to the wallet, usually within seconds.
  </Step>
  <Step title="You get the result">
    A `transfer.succeeded` or `transfer.failed` webhook. If a payout fails, the money goes back to your balance.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Where you can send money

| Network | `network` value | Wallet number |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wave | `wave` | 7 or 9 digits |
| Afrimoney | `afrimoney` | 7 or 9 digits |

To get the current list for your account, call `GET /v1/transfers/payout-channels`.

## The transfer object

```json
{
  "id": "45eb796c-e66a-442f-bba2-d282053f8883",
  "type": "mobile-money",
  "status": "completed",
  "amount": 100,
  "fee": 1,
  "currency": "GMD",
  "network": "afrimoney",
  "account_number": "7834567",
  "account_name": "Awa Jallow",
  "transfer_reference": "5Np7iVHrN",
  "balance_before": 995,
  "balance_after": 894,
  "note": "April supplies",
  "metadata": { "invoice_id": "inv_204" },
  "test_mode": true,
  "createdAt": "2025-05-05T21:12:52.839Z"
}
```

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `pending` | We're sending it. |
| `pending_review` | Our fraud checks are holding it. Review it in the dashboard. |
| `completed` | The money reached the wallet. |
| `failed` | It didn't go through. The money is back in your balance. |
| `cancelled` | It was stopped before sending. The money is back in your balance. |
| `reversed` | The money came back after it was sent. It's back in your balance. |

## Webhooks

| Event | Sent when |
| --- | --- |
| `transfer.succeeded` | The money reached the wallet. |
| `transfer.failed` | The payout failed. Your balance has been refunded. |
| `transfer.reversed` | The money came back, either because you reversed it, or because nobody claimed a Wave payout. Your balance has been refunded. |
| `transfer.flagged` | Our fraud checks are holding the payout for review. |

## Protect your balance

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Use a restricted key with payout limits">
    Create a key with only the `transfers` permission, a per-payout limit and a daily limit, and lock it to your servers' IP addresses. Even if it leaks, the damage is capped. See [API keys](/documentation/authentication#payout-limits).
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Always send an Idempotency-Key">
    If your request times out and you retry with the same key, we won't pay twice.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Watch for transfer.flagged">
    Flagged payouts need your review in the dashboard before more money can go to that number.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

---

# Send a mobile money payout
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/payouts/mobile-money

## What to send

| Field | Required | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `amount` | Yes | How much to send, in GMD. At least 10. |
| `currency` | Yes | `GMD`. |
| `network` | Yes | `wave` or `afrimoney`. |
| `account_number` | Yes | The wallet's phone number, 7 or 9 digits. |
| `beneficiary_name` | Yes | The wallet holder's name, at least 3 characters. |
| `narration` | No | A note for your records. |
| `metadata` | No | Your own data, like an invoice ID. |
| `callback_url` | No | An HTTPS URL to receive this payout's result. |

You also send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a unique value, like a UUID, for each payout. If you send the same request again with the same key, for example after a timeout, we return the first payout instead of paying twice.

<Tip>
  Not sure what it will cost? [Check the fee](/documentation/payouts/fees) first. The fee is taken from your balance on top of the amount.
</Tip>

## Send a payout

<CodeGroup>
```typescript nodejs
import ModemPay from "modem-pay";

const modemPay = new ModemPay("sk_test_...");

const response = await modemPay.transfers.initiate({
  amount: 100,
  currency: "GMD",
  network: "afrimoney",
  account_number: "7834567",
  beneficiary_name: "John Doe",
  narration: "Vendor payment for April supplies",
  metadata: {
    vendor_id: "vendor_001",
    invoice_id: "inv_204"
  }
}, "Idempotency-Key");
```
```python python
from modempay import ModemPay

modem_pay = ModemPay(api_key="sk_test_...")

response = modem_pay.transfers.initiate(
    params={
        "amount": 100,
        "currency": "GMD",
        "network": "afrimoney",
        "account_number": "7834567",
        "beneficiary_name": "John Doe",
        "narration": "Vendor payment for April supplies",
        "metadata": {"vendor_id": "vendor_001", "invoice_id": "inv_204"},
    },
    idempotency_key="Idempotency-Key"
)
```
```php php
use ModemPay\ModemPay;

$modemPay = new ModemPay('sk_test_...');

$transfer = $modemPay->transfers()->initiate([
    'amount' => 100,
    'currency' => 'GMD',
    'account_number' => '7834567',
    'network' => 'afrimoney',
    'beneficiary_name' => 'John Doe',
    'narration' => 'Vendor payment for April supplies',
    'metadata' => [
      'vendor_id' => 'vendor_001',
      'invoice_id' => 'inv_204',
    ],
], 'Idempotency-Key');
```
```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://api.modempay.com/v1/transfers \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: Idempotency-Key" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 100,
    "currency": "GMD",
    "network": "afrimoney",
    "account_number": "7834567",
    "beneficiary_name": "John Doe",
    "narration": "Vendor payment for April supplies",
    "metadata": {
      "vendor_id": "vendor_001",
      "invoice_id": "inv_204"
    }
  }'

```
</CodeGroup>

## What you get back

```typescript json
{
  "id": "45eb796c-e66a-442f-bba2-d282053f8883",
  "events": {},
  "business_id": "120c298f-b736-49c1-8220-8a8c84a5d8f3",
  "account_id": "199bf17b-0b5a-45c0-a5b0-1d29f5f173c9",
  "amount": 100,
  "currency": "GMD",
  "type": "mobile-money",
  "balance_before": 995,
  "balance_after": 894,
  "transfer_reference": "5Np7iVHrN",
  "test_mode": true,
  "status": "completed",
  "account_name": "John Doe",
  "network": "afrimoney",
  "mobile_number": "7834567",
  "account_number": "7834567",
  "note": "Vendor payment for April supplies",
  "fee": 1,
  "metadata": {
    "vendor_id": "vendor_001",
    "invoice_id": "inv_204"
  },
  "updatedAt": "2025-05-05T21:12:52.839Z",
  "createdAt": "2025-05-05T21:12:52.839Z",
  "merchant_id": null,
  "recipient_business_id": null,
  "bank": null,
  "amount_received": null,
  "otp": null
}
```

## Look up a payout

<CodeGroup>
```typescript nodejs
const transfer = await modemPay.transfers.retrieve("45eb796c...");
console.log(transfer.status); // e.g., 'completed'
```
```python python
transfer = modem_pay.transfers.retrieve("45eb796c...")
print(transfer["status"]); # e.g., 'completed'
```
```php php
$transfer = $modemPay->transfers()->retrieve("45eb796c...");
echo $transfer->status; # e.g., 'completed'
```
```bash cURL
curl -X GET https://api.modempay.com/v1/transfers/45eb796c... \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```
</CodeGroup>

## Fraud checks

Every payout goes through automatic fraud checks. If one looks unusual:

- its status becomes `pending_review`;
- you get an email and a `transfer.flagged` webhook;
- no more payouts can go to that number until you review it in the dashboard.

Review flagged payouts quickly so your normal payouts aren't held up.

## Common errors

| Message | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `Invalid transfer amount: … Must be at least 10.` | Send 10 GMD or more. |
| `Invalid account number format. Must be 7 or 9 digits` | Send only digits, no country code or spaces. |
| `Invalid network. Must be one of: afrimoney or wave` | Check the `network` value. |
| `429` with a `code` such as `RATE_LIMIT` | Slow down and retry later. See [Errors](/documentation/errors#error-codes-you-may-see). |

---

# Bulk payouts
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/payouts/bulk-payout

## What is a bulk payout?

A bulk payout means you send money to many people at once. You give us one list. We pay everyone on the list for you.

You can use it to:

- Pay salaries to your workers
- Send winnings to many players
- Pay your agents
- Refund many customers

## How it works

<Steps>
  <Step title="You send us a list">
    Each item on the list has an amount, a network (Wave or Afrimoney), a name,
    and an account number.
  </Step>
  <Step title="We take the money from your balance">
    We take the full amount for the whole list, plus fees, from your payout
    balance.
  </Step>
  <Step title="We pay each person">
    We send the payouts one by one. If one payout fails, we return that money to
    your balance. The other payouts still continue.
  </Step>
  <Step title="You see the results">
    You can check the status at any time. If you gave us a `callback_url`, we
    also send the final result to your server.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Note>Each payout must be at least **GMD 10**.</Note>

## Send a bulk payout

Send a `POST` request with your list.

<CodeGroup>

```typescript nodejs
const bulkPayout = await modempay.transfers.bulkPayout({
  payouts: [
    {
      amount: 1000,
      network: "wave",
      beneficiary_name: "Fatoumata Sanyang",
      account_number: "7900123",
      currency: "GMD",
    },
    {
      amount: 2500,
      network: "afrimoney",
      beneficiary_name: "Ebrima Jobe",
      account_number: "2100456",
      currency: "GMD",
    },
    {
      amount: 500,
      network: "wave",
      beneficiary_name: "Isatou Ceesay",
      account_number: "5600879",
      currency: "GMD",
    },
  ],
  batch_reference: "batch-20240601-demo",
});
```

```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://api.modempay.com/v1/transfers/bulk-transfers \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "payouts": [
      {
        "amount": 1000,
        "network": "wave",
        "beneficiary_name": "Fatoumata Sanyang",
        "account_number": "7900123",
        "currency": "GMD"
      },
      {
        "amount": 2500,
        "network": "afrimoney",
        "beneficiary_name": "Ebrima Jobe",
        "account_number": "2100456",
        "currency": "GMD"
      },
      {
        "amount": 500,
        "network": "wave",
        "beneficiary_name": "Isatou Ceesay",
        "account_number": "5600879",
        "currency": "GMD"
      }
    ],
    "batch_reference": "batch-20240601-demo"
  }'
```

</CodeGroup>

### What to send

<ParamField body="payouts" type="array" required>
  Your list of payouts. Each one needs:

  <Expandable title="payout fields">
    <ParamField body="amount" type="number" required>
      How much money to send. At least 10 GMD.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="network" type="string" required>
      Where the money goes. Use `wave` or `afrimoney`.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="beneficiary_name" type="string" required>
      The full name of the person getting the money.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="account_number" type="string" required>
      The person's mobile money number. 7 digits.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="currency" type="string" required>
      Always `GMD`.
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="batch_reference" type="string" required>
  Your own name for this list. Use a name you will remember, like
  `salaries-july-2026`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="callback_url" type="string">
  Optional. A link to your server. We send the final result there when we
  finish. Must start with `https`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="metadata" type="object">
  Optional. Any extra notes you want to keep with this batch.
</ParamField>

## Check a bulk payout

Use the `id` to see how the batch is going.

<CodeGroup>

```typescript nodejs
const bulkPayout = await modempay.transfers.retrieveBulkPayout(
  "e7b2c1a0-4f3d-4e2a-9b1c-2d3e4f5a6b7c",
);
```

```bash cURL
curl https://api.modempay.com/v1/transfers/bulk-transfers/e7b2c1a0-4f3d-4e2a-9b1c-2d3e4f5a6b7c \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx"
```

</CodeGroup>

### What you get back

```json
{
  "id": "e7b2c1a0-4f3d-4e2a-9b1c-2d3e4f5a6b7c",
  "business_id": "219a9b8b-d80e-4379-8c4e-40e3cdd8ec3d",
  "account_id": "f46f9d96-41e3-44d5-a102-4658bf419ad1",
  "test_mode": false,
  "status": "completed",
  "batch_reference": "batch-20240601-demo",
  "count": 3,
  "progress": 3,
  "success_count": 3,
  "failure_count": 0,
  "total_chargeable_amount": 4060,
  "total_fees": 60,
  "callback_url": "https://example.com/webhooks/modempay",
  "metadata": {},
  "payouts": [ ... ]
}
```

<ResponseField name="status" type="string">
  Where the batch is now. See the table below.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="count" type="number">
  How many payouts are in the batch.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="progress" type="number">
  How many payouts we have worked on so far. When `progress` is the same as
  `count`, the batch is done.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="success_count" type="number">
  How many payouts were sent with no problem.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="failure_count" type="number">
  How many payouts failed. Money from failed payouts goes back to your balance.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="total_chargeable_amount" type="number">
  The full amount we took from your balance, with fees.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="total_fees" type="number">
  The total fees for this batch.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="payouts" type="array">
  The list of payouts in this batch. Each one has its own status.
</ResponseField>

### Status meanings

| Status                | What it means                                             |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pending`             | We got your list. We have not started yet.                |
| `in-progress`         | We are sending the payouts now.                           |
| `completed`           | Every payout was sent.                                    |
| `failed`              | Every payout failed. All money went back to your balance. |
| `partially_completed` | Most payouts were sent. Some failed.                      |
| `partially_failed`    | Most payouts failed. Some were sent.                      |

<Tip>
  Money from failed payouts always goes back to your payout balance. Check
  `failure_count` to see how many failed. Then look at each payout in the list
  to see which ones failed, fix them, and send them again.
</Tip>

## Ways to use it

### Pay salaries

Pay your whole team with one request. Put every worker on the list. Use a clear name like `salaries-july-2026`. When the status is `completed`, everyone is paid.

### Pay winnings

Send winnings to many players at once. Add a `callback_url` so your system knows when we finish. Use `metadata` to save the game or draw ID.

### Pay agents

At the end of the week, put all agent payments in one list and send it. Use the check endpoint to show each agent their payment status in your app.

### Refund customers

Need to refund many people, for example after a cancelled event? Put all the refunds in one list instead of sending them one by one.

## Good to know

- **Check your balance first.** Your payout balance must cover the full list plus fees. If it is not enough, we reject the whole list.
- **One bad item stops the list.** We check every item before we start. If one item has a wrong account number or an amount below 10 GMD, we reject the whole list and send nothing. Fix the item and try again.
- **Failed payouts are refunded.** If a payout fails while we are sending it, the money goes back to your balance. You do not lose it.
- **Check any time.** You do not have to wait for the callback. Just call the check endpoint and compare `progress` with `count`.

---

# Payout fees
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/payouts/fees

Each payout has a fee that depends on the network and the amount. The fee is taken from your payout balance **on top of** the amount, so the recipient always gets the full amount you send.

## Check a fee

`POST /v1/transfers/fees` with the `amount`, `currency` and `network` you plan to use.

<CodeGroup>
```typescript nodejs
import ModemPay from "modem-pay";

const modemPay = new ModemPay("sk_test_...");

const feeResponse = await modemPay.transfers.fee({
  amount: 1000,
  currency: "GMD",
  network: "afrimoney"
});

console.log(`Payout fee: ${feeResponse.fee} ${feeResponse.currency}`);
console.log(`Total amount: ${feeResponse.amount} ${feeResponse.currency}`);
```
```python python
from modempay import ModemPay

modem_pay = ModemPay(api_key="sk_test_...")

fee_response = modem_pay.transfers.fee(
    {"amount": 1000, "currency": "GMD", "network": "afrimoney"}
)

print(f"Payout fee: {fee_response['fee']} {fee_response['currency']}")
print(f"Total amount: {fee_response['amount']} {fee_response['currency']}")
```
```php php
use ModemPay\ModemPay;

$modemPay = new ModemPay('sk_test_...');

$fee_response = $modemPay->transfers()->fee([
    'amount' => 1000,
    'currency' => 'GMD',
    'network' => 'afrimoney',
]);

print_r($fee_response);
```
```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://api.modempay.com/v1/transfers/fees \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 1000,
    "currency": "GMD",
    "network": "afrimoney"
  }'
```
</CodeGroup>

```json
{
  "fee": 5,
  "currency": "GMD",
  "network": "afrimoney",
  "amount": 1000
}
```

Here the recipient gets **1,000 GMD** and your balance goes down by **1,005 GMD**.

<Tip>
  For a [bulk payout](/documentation/payouts/bulk-payout), the response has `total_fees` and `total_chargeable_amount` for the whole batch.
</Tip>

---

# Reverse a payout
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/payouts/reversals

Sent money to the wrong number, or the wrong amount? You can ask Wave to return a completed payout. If Wave agrees, the money goes back to your payout balance.

## When you can reverse

- The payout went to **Wave**.
- Its status is `completed`.
- It was sent **no more than 3 days ago**.

Afrimoney payouts can't be reversed through the API. Contact the recipient, or email [info@modempay.com](mailto:info@modempay.com).

## Reverse it

Use the payout's `id` or its `transfer_reference`:

```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://api.modempay.com/v1/transfers/reverse/45eb796c-e66a-442f-bba2-d282053f8883 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```

This needs a key with the `transfers:write` permission.

If it works, the payout's status becomes `reversed`, the amount **and the fee** go back to your payout balance, and you get a `transfer.reversed` webhook.

If Wave refuses, for example because the money was already withdrawn, you get an error and nothing changes. The payout stays `completed`.

## Unclaimed Wave payouts

If a Wave payout goes to a number with no Wave account, Wave holds it. If nobody claims it, Wave returns it after about 15 days. We then put the money back in your payout balance and send `transfer.reversed`.

---

# Split payments
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/split-payments/overview

**Split Payments** share each payment between you and your partners automatically. No manual transfers, no spreadsheets.

Useful for marketplaces, schools, agencies, or any business that shares revenue.

## The building blocks

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card
    title="Sub-accounts"
    icon="user"
    href="/documentation/split-payments/sub-accounts"
  >
    One partner: who gets paid, where, and what percentage.
  </Card>
  <Card
    title="Sub-account groups"
    icon="users"
    href="/documentation/split-payments/sub-account-groups"
  >
    Several partners on one payment, each with its own percentage.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## How it works

<Steps>
  <Step title="Set up your partners">
    Create a [sub-account](/documentation/split-payments/sub-accounts) for each
    partner. To pay several on one payment, put them in a
    [group](/documentation/split-payments/sub-account-groups).
  </Step>
  <Step title="Attach to a payment">
    Pass `sub_account` or `sub_account_group` when you [create a payment
    intent](/documentation/split-payments/initialize-payment).
  </Step>
  <Step title="Get paid">
    When the customer pays, each partner's share goes to their balance and the
    rest goes to yours.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Example

A customer pays **1,000 GMD** and the customer covers the fee, so you receive the full 1,000 GMD.

|          | One sub-account (10%) | Group (30% + 40%) |
| -------- | --------------------- | ----------------- |
| Partners | 100 GMD               | 300 GMD + 400 GMD |
| You      | 900 GMD               | 300 GMD           |

If your business pays the fee instead, the percentages apply to what's left after the fee. See [how shares are calculated](/documentation/split-payments/sub-accounts#how-the-share-is-calculated).

---

# Sub-accounts
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/split-payments/sub-accounts

A **sub-account** is a partner who receives part of your payments. You set two things on it:

- **Who gets paid:** a mobile money account (`settlement_code` + `account_number`)
- **How much:** a `percentage` of each payment it is attached to

When a payment with a sub-account completes, Modem Pay moves that percentage into the sub-account's balance and keeps the rest in yours. No manual transfers.

<Tip>
  Need to pay **several partners** from one payment? Put them in a [Sub-Account
  Group](/documentation/split-payments/sub-account-groups).
</Tip>

## How it works

<Steps>
  <Step title="Create a sub-account">
    Give it a name, a percentage and where its money should go. You get back an
    `id`.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Attach it to a payment">
    Pass the `id` as `sub_account` when you [create a payment
    intent](/documentation/split-payments/initialize-payment).
  </Step>
  <Step title="Customer pays">
    The sub-account's share is added to its balance. The rest goes to your
    balance.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Sub-account is settled">
    Once its balance reaches **10 GMD**, it can be paid out to its account.
  </Step>
</Steps>

### How the share is calculated

The percentage is applied to **what you receive from the payment**, after Modem Pay's fee if your business pays the fee. If the customer pays the fee, it is applied to the full amount.

Shares are rounded to the nearest whole GMD, and every share is at least **1 GMD**.

| Payment   | Fee paid by | Modem Pay fee                          | You receive | Sub-account (10%) | Your balance |
| --------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------- | ------------ |
| 1,000 GMD | Business    | 20 GMD                                 | 980 GMD     | **98 GMD**        | **882 GMD**  |
| 1,000 GMD | Customer    | 20 GMD (added to the customer's total) | 1,000 GMD   | **100 GMD**       | **900 GMD**  |

<Note>Fees shown are examples. Your actual fee depends on your pricing.</Note>

---

## Create a sub-account

`POST /v1/sub-accounts`

| Field             | Type   | Required | Description                                               |
| ----------------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `business_name`   | string | Yes      | Name of the partner. Shown on your dashboard and reports. |
| `percentage`      | number | Yes      | Share of each payment, greater than 0 and at most 100.    |
| `settlement_code` | string | Yes      | Where the money is settled, e.g. `wave` or `afrimoney`.   |
| `account_number`  | string | Yes      | The partner's account number on that provider.            |

<CodeGroup>
```typescript nodejs
const subAccount = await modempay.subAccounts.create({
  business_name: "Hail-Ma",
  percentage: 10,
  settlement_code: "afrimoney",
  account_number: "7012345",
});

console.log(subAccount.id); // keep this, you'll attach it to payments

````
```python python
sub_account = mp.sub_accounts.create(
    params={
        "business_name": "Hail-Ma",
        "percentage": 10,
        "settlement_code": "afrimoney",
        "account_number": "7012345",
    }
)

print(sub_account["id"])
````

```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://api.modempay.com/v1/sub-accounts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "business_name": "Hail-Ma",
    "percentage": 10,
    "settlement_code": "afrimoney",
    "account_number": "7012345"
  }'
```

</CodeGroup>

<Warning>
  Double-check `account_number`. A wrong number means the sub-account's payout
  fails or goes to the wrong person.
</Warning>

## Retrieve a sub-account

`GET /v1/sub-accounts/:id`

Returns the sub-account, including its current `balance`.

<CodeGroup>
```typescript nodejs
const subAccount = await modempay.subAccounts.retrieve("5bfcc08....810b");
console.log(subAccount);
```

```python python
sub_account = mp.sub_accounts.retrieve("5bfcc08....810b")
print(sub_account)
```

```bash cURL
curl -X GET https://api.modempay.com/v1/sub-accounts/5bfcc08....810b \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
```

</CodeGroup>

## List sub-accounts

`GET /v1/sub-accounts`

| Query parameter | Default | Description                   |
| --------------- | ------- | ----------------------------- |
| `term`          | —       | Search by `business_name`.    |
| `limit`         | 15      | How many to return.           |
| `offset`        | 0       | How many to skip, for paging. |

<CodeGroup>
```typescript nodejs
const { data, meta } = await modempay.subAccounts.list();
console.log(meta.total);
```
```python python
result = mp.sub_accounts.list()
print(result["meta"]["total"])
```
```bash cURL
curl "https://api.modempay.com/v1/sub-accounts?term=hail&limit=15&offset=0" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```
</CodeGroup>

Response:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "5bfcc08....810b",
      "business_name": "Hail-Ma",
      "percentage": 10,
      "balance": 98,
      "active": true
    }
  ],
  "meta": { "total": 1 }
}
```

## Update a sub-account

`PUT /v1/sub-accounts/:id`

Send only the fields you want to change: `percentage`, `account_number`, `settlement_code` or `active`.

<CodeGroup>
```typescript nodejs
const updated = await modempay.subAccounts.update("5bfcc08....810b", {
  percentage: 15,
  account_number: "7016789",
});
```
```python python
updated = mp.sub_accounts.update(
    "5bfcc08....810b",
    {"percentage": 15, "account_number": "7016789"},
)
```
```bash cURL
curl -X PUT https://api.modempay.com/v1/sub-accounts/5bfcc08....810b \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "percentage": 15, "account_number": "7016789" }'
```
</CodeGroup>

- Changes apply to **future payments only**. Completed payments keep the split they were made with.
- Set `active` to `false` to pause a sub-account. New payment intents that use it are rejected.
- Changing a sub-account's `percentage` does **not** change its share inside a [group](/documentation/split-payments/sub-account-groups). Groups store their own percentages.

## Delete a sub-account

`DELETE /v1/sub-accounts/:id`

```bash cURL
curl -X DELETE https://api.modempay.com/v1/sub-accounts/5bfcc08....810b \
 -H "Authorization:Bearer sk_test_..."
```

A sub-account can only be deleted when its balance is **0**. Otherwise you get a `400`. To stop using one that still has money, set `active` to `false` instead.

---

## Rules at a glance

| Rule                         | Value                                                                        |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Percentage                   | Greater than 0, at most 100                                                  |
| Smallest share per payment   | 1 GMD                                                                        |
| Rounding                     | Nearest whole GMD                                                            |
| Balance needed before payout | 10 GMD                                                                       |
| Sub-accounts per payment     | 1 (use a [group](/documentation/split-payments/sub-account-groups) for more) |
| Test vs live                 | Test-mode sub-accounts only work with test keys, and live with live          |

---

# Sub-account groups
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/split-payments/sub-account-groups

A **sub-account group** lets one payment pay **several partners at once**. You put existing [sub-accounts](/documentation/split-payments/sub-accounts) in a group, give each one a percentage, and attach the group to a payment.

Good for: a marketplace paying a seller and a delivery rider, a school sharing fees between departments, an agency paying several collaborators.

## How it works

<Steps>
  <Step title="Create the sub-accounts">
    Each partner needs a
    [sub-account](/documentation/split-payments/sub-accounts#create-a-sub-account)
    first.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Create a group">
    List the sub-accounts and the percentage each one gets. The percentages must
    add up to **100% or less**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Attach the group to a payment">
    Pass the group's `id` as `sub_account_group` when you [create a payment
    intent](/documentation/split-payments/initialize-payment).
  </Step>
  <Step title="Customer pays">
    Every member's share goes to its balance. Whatever is left goes to your
    balance.
  </Step>
</Steps>

### Example

A customer pays 1,000 GMD. Your business pays a 20 GMD fee, so you receive **980 GMD**. Your group has two members:

| Member              | Percentage | Share of 980 GMD |
| ------------------- | ---------- | ---------------- |
| Seller              | 30%        | **294 GMD**      |
| Rider               | 40%        | **392 GMD**      |
| You (the remainder) | 30%        | **294 GMD**      |

Shares are worked out the same way as for a single sub-account: on what you receive after the fee if your business pays it (the full amount if the customer pays), rounded to the nearest whole GMD, at least **1 GMD** each.

<Note>
  On very small payments, the 1 GMD minimum and rounding could add up to more
  than the payment. When that happens, the largest shares are reduced so the
  members never get more than the payment itself.
</Note>

---

## Create a group

`POST /v1/sub-account-groups`

| Field         | Type    | Required | Description                                             |
| ------------- | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`        | string  | Yes      | Up to 120 characters. Must be unique among your groups. |
| `description` | string  | No       | A note for yourself.                                    |
| `members`     | array   | Yes      | 1 to 50 members (see below).                            |
| `active`      | boolean | No       | Defaults to `true`.                                     |

Each item in `members`:

| Field            | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sub_account_id` | string | Yes      | ID of an active sub-account. Each one can appear only once.                                                                                       |
| `percentage`     | number | No       | This member's share in **this group**, greater than 0 and at most 100, up to 2 decimals. If left out, the sub-account's own `percentage` is used. |

<CodeGroup>
```typescript nodejs
const group = await modempay.subAccountGroups.create({
  name: "Marketplace order split",
  description: "Seller and rider",
  members: [
    { sub_account_id: "5bfcc08....810b", percentage: 30 },
    { sub_account_id: "a91e2c4....77d0", percentage: 40 },
  ],
});

console.log(group.id); // pass this as sub_account_group on payment intents

````
```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://api.modempay.com/v1/sub-account-groups \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Marketplace order split",
    "description": "Seller and rider",
    "members": [
      { "sub_account_id": "5bfcc08....810b", "percentage": 30 },
      { "sub_account_id": "a91e2c4....77d0", "percentage": 40 }
    ]
  }'
````

</CodeGroup>

Response (`201`):

```json
{
  "id": "c3d1f0a....e21f",
  "name": "Marketplace order split",
  "description": "Seller and rider",
  "active": true,
  "members": [
    {
      "sub_account_id": "5bfcc08....810b",
      "percentage": "30.00",
      "sub_account": {
        "id": "5bfcc08....810b",
        "business_name": "Seller",
        "settlement_code": "wave",
        "account_number": "7012345",
        "active": true
      }
    },
    {
      "sub_account_id": "a91e2c4....77d0",
      "percentage": "40.00",
      "sub_account": {
        "id": "a91e2c4....77d0",
        "business_name": "Rider",
        "settlement_code": "afrimoney",
        "account_number": "7016789",
        "active": true
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<Tip>
  A member's percentage belongs to the group, not the sub-account. The same
  sub-account can have 30% in one group and 50% in another, and changing the
  sub-account's own percentage won't affect either group.
</Tip>

## Retrieve a group

`GET /v1/sub-account-groups/:id`

Returns the group with its members and their sub-account details.

<CodeGroup>
  ```typescript nodejs 
const group = await modempay.subAccountGroups.retrieve("c3d1f0a....e21f"); 
```

```bash cURL
curl https://api.modempay.com/v1/sub-account-groups/c3d1f0a....e21f \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```

</CodeGroup>

## List groups

`GET /v1/sub-account-groups`

| Query parameter | Default | Description                                     |
| --------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `term`          | —       | Search by name. In Node, pass it as `search`.   |
| `active`        | —       | `true` or `false` to filter. Leave out for all. |
| `limit`         | 15      | How many to return, up to 100.                  |
| `offset`        | 0       | How many to skip, for paging.                   |

<CodeGroup>
```typescript nodejs
const { data, meta } = await modempay.subAccountGroups.list({
  search: "marketplace",
  active: true,
  limit: 15,
  offset: 0,
});
```
```bash cURL
curl "https://api.modempay.com/v1/sub-account-groups?term=marketplace&active=true&limit=15&offset=0" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```
</CodeGroup>

Response: `{ "data": [ ...groups ], "meta": { "total": 3 } }`

## Update a group

`PUT /v1/sub-account-groups/:id`

Send only what you want to change: `name`, `description`, `active` or `members`.

<Warning>
  `members` **replaces the whole list**. To add one partner, send all the
  existing members plus the new one. The new list is checked again against the
  100% limit.
</Warning>

<CodeGroup>
```typescript nodejs
const group = await modempay.subAccountGroups.update("c3d1f0a....e21f", {
  members: [
    { sub_account_id: "5bfcc08....810b", percentage: 30 },
    { sub_account_id: "a91e2c4....77d0", percentage: 35 },
    { sub_account_id: "e7b4d19....03ac", percentage: 10 },
  ],
});
```
```bash cURL
curl -X PUT https://api.modempay.com/v1/sub-account-groups/c3d1f0a....e21f \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "members": [
      { "sub_account_id": "5bfcc08....810b", "percentage": 30 },
      { "sub_account_id": "a91e2c4....77d0", "percentage": 35 },
      { "sub_account_id": "e7b4d19....03ac", "percentage": 10 }
    ]
  }'
```
</CodeGroup>

Changes apply to **payments completed after the update**. Completed payments keep the split they were made with.

## Deactivate a group

`DELETE /v1/sub-account-groups/:id`

<CodeGroup>
  ```typescript nodejs 
  const group = await modempay.subAccountGroups.delete("c3d1f0a....e21f");
  console.log(group.active); // false 
```

```bash cURL
curl -X DELETE https://api.modempay.com/v1/sub-account-groups/c3d1f0a....e21f \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```

</CodeGroup>

This **deactivates** the group rather than deleting it, so past payments still show which group they used. Returns the group with `"active": false`. To use it again, update it with `"active": true`.

---

## What happens when something changes mid-payment

A payment intent is checked when it is created, but the split happens when the customer actually pays. If things change in between:

| Situation                                        | What happens                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Group is inactive when you create the intent     | Intent is rejected with `400`                                                                 |
| Group is deactivated after the intent is created | Payment still succeeds; **you keep the full amount**                                          |
| A member's sub-account is deactivated            | Payment still succeeds; that member's share **stays with you**, the others are paid as normal |
| Group's members or percentages are updated       | The split uses the group as it is **when the payment completes**                              |

The customer's payment never fails because of a group change.

## Errors

| Status | When                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `400`  | Percentages add up to more than 100%, a percentage is out of range, a sub-account is listed twice, a sub-account is inactive, no members, or more than 50 members |
| `404`  | The group or one of the sub-accounts doesn't exist, or belongs to another business, account or mode                                                               |
| `409`  | You already have a group with this name                                                                                                                           |

## Rules at a glance

| Rule                                        | Value                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Members per group                           | 1 to 50                                                       |
| Total of percentages                        | At most 100%                                                  |
| Percentage per member                       | Greater than 0, at most 100, up to 2 decimals                 |
| Smallest share per member                   | 1 GMD                                                         |
| Rounding                                    | Nearest whole GMD                                             |
| Group and `sub_account` on the same payment | The group is used, `sub_account` is ignored                   |
| Test vs live                                | Groups and their members must be in the same mode as your key |

---

# Split a payment
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/split-payments/initialize-payment

To split a payment, attach a sub-account or a sub-account group when you create the **Payment Intent**. The split happens automatically when the customer pays.

| To pay           | Pass                | Example                          |
| ---------------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| One partner      | `sub_account`       | Your platform and one seller     |
| Several partners | `sub_account_group` | A seller, a rider and a referrer |

## Split with one sub-account

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs
const paymentIntent = await modempay.paymentIntents.create({
  amount: 1000,
  sub_account: "5bfcc08....810b",
});
```
```python python
payment_intent = modem_pay.payment_intents.create(params={
    "amount": 1000,
    "sub_account": "5bfcc08....810b",
})
```
```bash cURL
curl -X POST "https://api.modempay.com/v1/payments" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "amount": 1000,
      "sub_account": "5bfcc08....810b",
      "from_sdk": false
    }
  }'
```
</CodeGroup>

The sub-account's `percentage` decides its share.

## Split with a group

<CodeGroup>
```javascript nodejs
const paymentIntent = await modempay.paymentIntents.create({
  amount: 1000,
  sub_account_group: "c3d1f0a....e21f",
});
```
```python python
payment_intent = modem_pay.payment_intents.create(params={
    "amount": 1000,
    "sub_account_group": "c3d1f0a....e21f",
})
```
```bash cURL
curl -X POST "https://api.modempay.com/v1/payments" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "amount": 1000,
      "sub_account_group": "c3d1f0a....e21f",
      "from_sdk": false
    }
  }'
```
</CodeGroup>

Each member gets the percentage set for it in the group.

<Note>If you pass both, **the group wins** and `sub_account` is ignored.</Note>

## What each party receives

Shares are calculated on what you receive from the payment: after Modem Pay's fee if your business pays it, or the full amount if the customer pays it. Shares are rounded to the nearest whole GMD, with at least 1 GMD each.

**Example:** a 1,000 GMD payment, your business pays a 20 GMD fee, so you receive 980 GMD.

| Setup                                | Partners get      | Your balance |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------- | ------------ |
| `sub_account` at 10%                 | 98 GMD            | 882 GMD      |
| `sub_account_group` with 30% and 40% | 294 GMD + 392 GMD | 294 GMD      |

## Before you create the intent

The sub-account or group must:

- Exist and be **active**
- Belong to the same business and account as your API key
- Be in the same mode as your key (test with test, live with live)

If not, the intent is rejected with `400` and no payment is started.

The payment intent and the transaction both show the `sub_account` or `sub_account_group` that was used, so you can match payments to splits in your own records.

---

# Stablecoins overview
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/stablecoins/overview

Stablecoins are digital dollars. One USDT or one USDC is meant to be worth one
US dollar, so their value stays steady, unlike other cryptocurrencies. People
hold them in crypto wallets and exchange apps, and can send them anywhere in
seconds.

Modem Pay lets you work with stablecoins without running any crypto
infrastructure. We create the payment addresses, watch for the money, and
settle you in dalasi (GMD).

## What you can do

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Accept stablecoin payments" icon="cart-shopping" href="/documentation/stablecoins/accept-payments">
    Charge a customer in USD and let them pay with USDT or USDC on a hosted
    payment page.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Convert stablecoins to dalasi" icon="arrow-right-arrow-left" href="/documentation/stablecoins/convert-to-dalasi">
    Send USDT or USDC and receive GMD in your balance or a mobile money wallet.
    Also called an off-ramp.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Check prices first" icon="calculator" href="/documentation/stablecoins/price-estimates">
    See how much GMD an amount is worth, or how much to send for a GMD amount,
    before creating anything.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Resell conversions" icon="handshake" href="/documentation/stablecoins/resellers">
    Offer conversions on your own platform and earn your own markup.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## Supported coins and networks

A stablecoin lives on a **network** (a blockchain). The same coin on two
different networks is not interchangeable, so the coin and the network must
always match what the payer's wallet sends.

| Coin | Network | `network` value | Minimum conversion | Modem Pay network fee | Arrives in |
|------|---------|-----------------|--------------------|-----------------------|------------|
| USDT | Tron (TRC20) | `TRC20` | $25 | $1.50 | about 1 minute |
| USDC | Arc | `ARC` | $5 | none | under 1 second |

The minimums and network fee apply to [conversions to dalasi](/documentation/stablecoins/convert-to-dalasi).
The **network fee** covers what it costs us to move the money on that
network. It's added once per conversion and included in the amount to send.
The payer's own wallet may also charge a small sending fee.

<Tip>
  For USDC, use **Arc**. It's Circle's own network, there's no network fee,
  the minimum is lower, and payments are final in under a second.
</Tip>

<Warning>
  **Sending on the wrong network can lose the money.** USDT sent on Ethereum to
  a Tron address, or USDC sent on another network to an Arc address, will not
  reach us. Always tell the payer both the coin **and** the network.
</Warning>

## Words you'll see

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Stablecoin">
    A digital currency designed to stay at the same value as a normal currency.
    USDT and USDC both track the US dollar.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Network (blockchain)">
    The system a stablecoin moves on, such as Tron or Arc. The payer chooses it
    in their wallet when sending.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Payment address">
    A one-time address we create for each payment, shown as `pay_address`. It
    looks like `T…` on Tron and `0x…` on Arc. Only send the requested coin on
    the requested network to it.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Off-ramp (conversion)">
    Turning stablecoins into local money. In these docs we call it
    **converting to dalasi**. The API paths still use the word `offramp`.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Rate">
    How many dalasi you get for one US dollar (`gmd_rate`). It's locked when you
    create a conversion, so price changes after that don't affect it.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Partial payment">
    When less than the full amount arrives. We credit you for what arrived and
    wait for the rest. See [Partial payments](/documentation/stablecoins/convert-to-dalasi#partial-payments).
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Before you start

- Stablecoin features work in **live mode only**. Use a live API key.
- All stablecoin endpoints live under `https://api.modempay.com/v1/minting`.
- Set a `callback_url`, or a webhook in your dashboard, so you hear about
  payments as they arrive. See the [Webhooks guide](/documentation/core/webhooks).

---

# Accept stablecoin payments
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/stablecoins/accept-payments

Create a payment request, send your customer to the hosted page, and we tell
you when the money arrives. The customer picks the coin and network on the
page, so you never handle wallets or addresses.

<Note>Stablecoin payments work in live mode only. Use a live API key.</Note>

## How it works

<Steps>
  <Step title="Create a payment request">
    Tell us how much to collect, in USD or GMD. We return a `link`.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Send your customer to the link">
    They choose USDT or USDC and a network (for example USDC on Arc), then pay
    from their wallet.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Get notified">
    We send a `charge.succeeded` update each time money arrives, with the
    running total.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Create a payment request

`POST /v1/minting/intents`

<ParamField body="amount" type="number" required>
  How much to collect. Minimum **5 USD** (or the GMD equivalent).
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="currency" type="string" default="USD">
  `USD` or `GMD`. A GMD amount is converted to USD at the current rate, so the
  request is always held in USD.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="metadata" type="object">
  Your own data, such as an order number. Returned to you unchanged in every
  update.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="callback_url" type="string">
  Where we send updates for this payment.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="expires_at" type="string">
  Optional deadline for the payment, in ISO 8601 format.
</ParamField>

<CodeGroup>

```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://api.modempay.com/v1/minting/intents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 20,
    "metadata": { "order_id": "ORD-1042" }
  }'
```

```typescript nodejs
const request = await modempay.quoteIntents.create({
  amount: 20,
  metadata: { order_id: "ORD-1042" },
});
```

</CodeGroup>

### Response

```json
{
  "id": "6f1a2b3c-4d5e-6f70-8192-a3b4c5d6e7f8",
  "status": "pending",
  "amount": 20,
  "currency": "USD",
  "metadata": { "order_id": "ORD-1042" },
  "link": "https://checkout.modempay.com/pay/quote/6f1a2b3c-4d5e-6f70-8192-a3b4c5d6e7f8",
  "createdAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
}
```

Send your customer to `link`.

## What the customer sees

The hosted page lists the coins and networks we support, including USDT on
Tron and USDC on Arc (see
[supported coins and networks](/documentation/stablecoins/overview#supported-coins-and-networks)).
After they choose, the page shows the exact amount, the address and a QR code,
and updates as soon as the payment arrives.

## Knowing when you've been paid

A customer can pay in one transfer or several, and can pay less than the full
amount. Two fields in each update tell you where things stand:

| Field                         | Meaning                                                                  |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `payload.amount`              | Total received so far, in USD. Grows with each transfer.                 |
| `payload.metadata.usd_amount` | The amount you asked for, in USD.                                        |
| `payload.status`              | `partially_paid` until the total reaches `usd_amount`, then `completed`. |

**The payment is complete when `status` is `completed`.**

## Updates (webhooks)

We send `charge.succeeded` every time money arrives.

```json
{
  "event": "charge.succeeded",
  "payload": {
    "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
    "status": "partially_paid",
    "amount": 10,
    "currency": "USD",
    "payment_method": "ARC",
    "reference": "MP-XXXXXXXX-XXXXXX-XXXXXXXX",
    "metadata": {
      "order_id": "ORD-1042",
      "usd_amount": 20,
      "gmd_rate": 74.8814,
      "fee": 0.2,
      "fee_currency": "USD",
      "fee_bearer": "business",
      "payment_history": [
        {
          "amount_paid_usd": 10,
          "amount_paid_gmd": 748,
          "timestamp": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Here \$10 of \$20 has arrived, so `status` is `partially_paid`. When the other
$10 arrives you get another `charge.succeeded` with `amount: 20` and
`status: "completed"`.

`payment_method` is the network the customer paid on (`TRC20` or `ARC`).
`payment_history` lists each transfer separately.

<Warning>
  You can receive several updates for the same payment. Match on the payment
  `id` (or your own `metadata` reference), treat `amount` as a running total,
  and make sure processing the same update twice doesn't double-count.
</Warning>

To check an update really came from Modem Pay, see the
[Webhooks guide](/documentation/core/webhooks).

## List and look up payment requests

```bash List
curl https://api.modempay.com/v1/minting/intents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
```

```bash Look up one
curl https://api.modempay.com/v1/minting/intents/6f1a2b3c-4d5e-6f70-8192-a3b4c5d6e7f8 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
```

## Checklist

- Save the request `id` and your own reference in `metadata`.
- Fulfil the order when an update arrives with `status: "completed"`.
- Handle repeated updates for the same `id` safely.
- Use `payment_history` if you need the individual transfers.

---

# Convert stablecoins to dalasi
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/stablecoins/convert-to-dalasi

Converting turns stablecoins into dalasi (GMD). You create a conversion, we give
you an address and the exact amount to send, and once the money arrives we pay
out the dalasi to your Modem Pay balance or straight to a Wave or Afrimoney
wallet.

You can size a conversion either way:

- **By the dalasi you want**, with `gmd_amount`: "I need 5,000 GMD, how much
  USDT do I send?"
- **By the stablecoin you have**, with `pay_amount`: "I have 100 USDC, how much
  GMD do I get?"

<Note>Conversions work in live mode only. Use a live API key.</Note>

## How it works

<Steps>
  <Step title="Create a conversion">
    Tell us the amount, the coin, the network and where the dalasi should go. We
    lock the rate and return a payment address.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Send the stablecoin">
    Send exactly `pay_amount` of `pay_currency` on `network` to `pay_address`
    within **10 minutes**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Receive the dalasi">
    As soon as the payment is confirmed, we credit `gmd_amount` to your balance
    or pay it to the mobile money wallet you chose.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Tip>
  Want to show a price before committing? Use the [price
  estimate](/documentation/stablecoins/price-estimates) endpoint. It returns the
  same numbers without creating a payment address.
</Tip>

## Create a conversion

`POST /v1/minting/offramp`

Send **either** `gmd_amount` **or** `pay_amount`, not both.

<ParamField body="gmd_amount" type="number">
  The dalasi you want to receive. We work out how much stablecoin to send.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="pay_amount" type="number">
  The stablecoin amount you will send, in USD (for example `100` for 100 USDT).
  We work out the dalasi you receive, after fees.
</ParamField>

<Info>
  **Minimums depend on the network:** \$25 on Tron and \$5 on Arc, measured on
  the amount sent. Requests must also be worth at least 400 GMD. Anything
  smaller is rejected with a message stating the minimum.
</Info>

<ParamField body="pay_currency" type="string" default="USDT">
  The coin you'll send: `USDT` or `USDC`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="network" type="string" default="TRC20">
  The network you'll send on: `TRC20` (Tron) or `ARC`. Arc supports USDC only.
  See [supported coins and
  networks](/documentation/stablecoins/overview#supported-coins-and-networks).
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="destination" type="string" default="modempay_balance">
  Where the dalasi goes: `modempay_balance` or `mobile_money`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="payout_method" type="object">
  Required when `destination` is `mobile_money`. The wallet to pay.

  <Expandable title="payout_method">
    <ParamField body="network" type="string" required>
      `wave` or `afrimoney`.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="account_number" type="string" required>
      The 7-digit wallet number, for example `7000000`.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="account_name" type="string" required>
      The name on the wallet (at least 3 characters).
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="callback_url" type="string">
  Where we send updates for this conversion. See [Updates](#updates-webhooks).
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="markup_config" type="object">
  Only for resellers. See [Resell
  conversions](/documentation/stablecoins/resellers).
</ParamField>

### Example: you want 5,000 GMD

<CodeGroup>

```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://api.modempay.com/v1/minting/offramp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "gmd_amount": 5000,
    "pay_currency": "USDT",
    "network": "TRC20"
  }'
```

```typescript nodejs
const conversion = await modempay.offramp.create({
  gmd_amount: 5000,
  pay_currency: "USDT",
  network: "TRC20",
});
```

</CodeGroup>

### Example: you have 100 USDC on Arc

<CodeGroup>

```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://api.modempay.com/v1/minting/offramp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "pay_amount": 100,
    "pay_currency": "USDC",
    "network": "ARC"
  }'
```

```typescript nodejs
const conversion = await modempay.offramp.create({
  pay_amount: 100,
  pay_currency: "USDC",
  network: "ARC",
});
```

</CodeGroup>

The payment request is for exactly `100` USDC, and `gmd_amount` in the response
tells you the dalasi you'll receive.

### Example: pay the dalasi to a Wave wallet

<CodeGroup>

```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://api.modempay.com/v1/minting/offramp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "gmd_amount": 5000,
    "destination": "mobile_money",
    "payout_method": {
      "network": "wave",
      "account_number": "7000000",
      "account_name": "Awa Jallow"
    }
  }'
```

```typescript nodejs
const conversion = await modempay.offramp.create({
  gmd_amount: 5000,
  destination: "mobile_money",
  payout_method: {
    network: "wave",
    account_number: "7000000",
    account_name: "Awa Jallow",
  },
});
```

</CodeGroup>

### Response

```json
{
  "id": "b7c93f02-1a4e-4d8c-9f31-2e6a5d8c41bb",
  "reference": "MP-XXXXXXXX-XXXXXX-XXXXXXXX",
  "status": "pending",
  "gmd_amount": 7009,
  "gmd_rate": 71.1425,
  "fee": 1.47,
  "fee_currency": "USD",
  "pay_amount": 100,
  "pay_currency": "USDC",
  "network": "ARC",
  "pay_address": "0x3158Fb72808f76A91a0FcDd0Ece7126265b69f3B",
  "invoice_expires_at": "2026-01-01T00:10:00.000Z",
  "actually_paid": 0,
  "destination": "modempay_balance",
  "payout_method": null,
  "markup_share_usd": 0,
  "createdAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
}
```

| Field                                     | What it means                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pay_address`                             | Where to send the stablecoin.                                                                        |
| `pay_amount` + `pay_currency` + `network` | Exactly what to send, and on which network.                                                          |
| `gmd_amount`                              | The dalasi you receive once fully paid.                                                              |
| `gmd_rate`                                | Dalasi per US dollar, locked for this conversion.                                                    |
| `fee`                                     | Modem Pay's fee in USD, already included in `pay_amount`. On Tron it includes the $1.50 network fee. |
| `invoice_expires_at`                      | Send before this time (10 minutes after creation).                                                   |
| `actually_paid`                           | How much has arrived so far, in USD.                                                                 |

## Statuses

| Status      | Meaning                                                                                          |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `pending`   | Created. Waiting for the stablecoin.                                                             |
| `underpaid` | Part of the amount has arrived. We've credited that part and are waiting for the rest.           |
| `paid`      | The full amount arrived. `gmd_amount` has been credited.                                         |
| `overpaid`  | More than `pay_amount` arrived. `gmd_amount` has been credited. Contact support about the extra. |
| `expired`   | Nothing (or not enough) arrived within 10 minutes.                                               |

## Partial payments

A payer may send less than `pay_amount`, or split it across several transfers.
You don't lose anything:

- Each transfer is credited as it arrives, in proportion. If half of
  `pay_amount` arrives, you get half of `gmd_amount`.
- When the rest arrives, you get the remainder, so the total is exactly
  `gmd_amount`.
- You never receive more than `gmd_amount` for a conversion.

Follow progress with `status` and `actually_paid`, or wait for the
[updates](#updates-webhooks) we send.

<Warning>
  Send the payment within 10 minutes. Money that arrives after the conversion
  expires isn't converted automatically. Contact support with the `reference`
  and it will be resolved manually.
</Warning>

## Look up a conversion

`GET /v1/minting/ramps/{id}`

```bash cURL
curl https://api.modempay.com/v1/minting/ramps/b7c93f02-1a4e-4d8c-9f31-2e6a5d8c41bb \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
```

Returns the same object as when you created it, with the latest `status`,
`actually_paid` and a timeline in `events`.

## Updates (webhooks)

When money arrives, we send an update to your `callback_url` (and your
dashboard webhook). The event name follows the status:

| Event            | When                                         |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `ramp.underpaid` | Part of the amount arrived and was credited. |
| `ramp.paid`      | The full amount arrived and was credited.    |
| `ramp.overpaid`  | More than the full amount arrived.           |

The payload is the conversion object shown above. You can get several updates
for one conversion as transfers come in, so match on `id` or `reference` and
treat `actually_paid` as the running total. Expiry doesn't send an update; look
the conversion up if you need to confirm it.

To check an update really came from Modem Pay, see the
[Webhooks guide](/documentation/core/webhooks).

## If a mobile money payout fails

When `destination` is `mobile_money`, the dalasi first lands in your Modem Pay
balance and is then paid to the wallet. If the wallet payout fails (wrong
number, provider outage), the dalasi **stays in your balance**. It's never
lost, and you can pay it out again from the dashboard or the
[Payouts API](/documentation/payouts/overview).

## Good to know

- The rate is locked when you create the conversion and doesn't change while it
  waits for payment.
- Fees are included in `pay_amount`. The `fee` field shows how much of it is
  Modem Pay's: a percentage (capped at $2), plus the network fee on Tron.
- With `pay_amount`, you receive the largest whole number of dalasi that
  amount covers after fees. Any fraction under 1 GMD isn't credited.
- Network values are case-insensitive: `ARC`, `arc` and `Arc` all work.

---

# Price estimates
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/stablecoins/price-estimates

Use an estimate to show your user a price before they commit. An estimate uses
the same rate, fees and limits as a real conversion, but creates nothing: no
payment address, no record and no expiry clock.

## Get an estimate

`GET /v1/minting/offramp/estimate`

Send **either** `gmd_amount` **or** `pay_amount`.

<ParamField query="gmd_amount" type="number">
  The dalasi you want to receive. Returns how much stablecoin to send.
</ParamField>

<ParamField query="pay_amount" type="number">
  The stablecoin amount you'll send, in USD. Returns the dalasi you'll receive.
</ParamField>

<ParamField query="pay_currency" type="string" default="USDT">
  `USDT` or `USDC`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField query="network" type="string" default="TRC20">
  `TRC20` or `ARC`.
</ParamField>

<CodeGroup>

```bash How much GMD for 50 USDC?
curl "https://api.modempay.com/v1/minting/offramp/estimate?pay_amount=50&pay_currency=USDC&network=ARC" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
```

```bash How much USDT for 5,000 GMD?
curl "https://api.modempay.com/v1/minting/offramp/estimate?gmd_amount=5000&pay_currency=USDT&network=TRC20" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
```

</CodeGroup>

### Response

```json
{
  "gmd_amount": 3504,
  "gmd_rate": 71.1425,
  "effective_rate": 70.08,
  "usd_amount": 49.26,
  "fee": 0.74,
  "fee_currency": "USD",
  "pay_amount": 50,
  "pay_currency": "USDC",
  "network": "ARC",
  "network_fee_estimate": "<$0.01",
  "network_fee_usd": 0,
  "min_amount_usd": 5,
  "confirmation_time": "<1 sec",
  "expires_at": "2026-01-01T00:05:00.000Z"
}
```

| Field | What it means |
|-------|---------------|
| `gmd_amount` | Dalasi received. |
| `pay_amount` | Stablecoin to send, fees included. |
| `gmd_rate` | Dalasi per US dollar before the fee. |
| `effective_rate` | Dalasi per US dollar after the fee (`gmd_amount ÷ pay_amount`). Use this when comparing prices. |
| `usd_amount` | The dollar value converted, without the fee. |
| `fee` | Modem Pay's fee, in USD, including any network fee. |
| `network_fee_usd` | The flat network fee for this network ($1.50 on Tron, none on Arc). Already part of `fee`. |
| `min_amount_usd` | The smallest amount you can send on this network. |
| `network_fee_estimate` | Roughly what the payer's wallet charges to send on this network. Paid by the payer, not deducted by us. |
| `expires_at` | How long to treat the price as fresh (5 minutes). |

<Note>
  An estimate doesn't hold the price. Rates move, so the conversion you create
  afterwards can differ slightly. The amounts in the conversion response are
  the ones that count.
</Note>

## Full quote

`POST /v1/minting/offramp/quote` takes exactly the same body as
[creating a conversion](/documentation/stablecoins/convert-to-dalasi#create-a-conversion),
including `destination`, `payout_method` and `markup_config`, and returns the
full conversion object without creating it. Use it to check a reseller markup
or a mobile money payout before going live.

```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://api.modempay.com/v1/minting/offramp/quote \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "pay_amount": 100,
    "pay_currency": "USDC",
    "network": "ARC",
    "markup_config": { "type": "percentage", "value": 2 }
  }'
```

---

# Resell conversions
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/stablecoins/resellers

If you run your own app or exchange desk, you can offer conversions to your
users under your own brand and add a markup. Your user pays the conversion plus
your markup; Modem Pay handles the stablecoin, the conversion and the payout,
and credits your markup to your balance.

<Note>
  This page adds one field, `markup_config`, to a normal conversion. Everything
  in [Convert stablecoins to dalasi](/documentation/stablecoins/convert-to-dalasi)
  still applies.
</Note>

## How the price is built

```
pay_amount = conversion (gmd_amount at the rate) + Modem Pay fee + your markup
```

- The **conversion** and **fee** work exactly like a normal conversion.
- Your **markup** is added on top. Your user pays it, and you keep it.

## markup_config

<ParamField body="markup_config" type="object">
  <Expandable title="markup_config">
    <ParamField body="type" type="string" required>
      `fixed` for a flat USD amount, or `percentage` for a percent of the
      converted amount.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="value" type="number" required>
      For `fixed`, USD (`4` means $4). For `percentage`, a percent (`2` means
      2%).
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

<Warning>
  Your markup can be at most **10% of the converted amount**. A request above
  that is rejected with the maximum allowed, so check small amounts carefully
  when using a `fixed` markup.
</Warning>

## Example

A 2% markup on a 5,000 GMD conversion paid to the user's Wave wallet:

<CodeGroup>

```bash cURL
curl -X POST https://api.modempay.com/v1/minting/offramp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "gmd_amount": 5000,
    "destination": "mobile_money",
    "payout_method": {
      "network": "wave",
      "account_number": "7000000",
      "account_name": "Awa Jallow"
    },
    "markup_config": { "type": "percentage", "value": 2 }
  }'
```

```typescript nodejs
const conversion = await modempay.offramp.create({
  gmd_amount: 5000,
  destination: "mobile_money",
  payout_method: {
    network: "wave",
    account_number: "7000000",
    account_name: "Awa Jallow",
  },
  markup_config: { type: "percentage", value: 2 },
});
```

</CodeGroup>

You can also size it by what the user sends, with `pay_amount` instead of
`gmd_amount`. The markup comes out of that amount, and `gmd_amount` in the
response shows what the user receives.

### Response (markup fields)

```json
{
  "gmd_amount": 5000,
  "fee": 2.55,
  "pay_amount": 74.05,
  "pay_currency": "USDT",
  "markup_share_usd": 1.4,
  "markup_config": { "type": "percentage", "value": 2 },
  "status": "pending"
}
```

`pay_amount` includes your markup, and `markup_share_usd` is what you earn, in
USD.

<Tip>
  Check the price your user will see with a
  [full quote](/documentation/stablecoins/price-estimates#full-quote) before
  creating the conversion.
</Tip>

## How you get paid

- Your user's dalasi (`gmd_amount`) goes to their wallet or your balance, as
  set by `destination`.
- Your markup is credited to **your Modem Pay balance**, as a separate entry,
  even when the user's dalasi goes to a mobile money wallet.
- With partial payments, the user's dalasi and your markup are credited in the
  same proportion as the money arrives, and complete together.

## Good to know

- The markup is locked when the conversion is created and doesn't change with
  the rate.
- The Modem Pay fee applies to the conversion as usual; your markup is yours.

---

# Virtual terminals
Source: https://docs.modempay.com/documentation/virtual-terminal

Virtual Terminals turn any counter into a smart payment station.

Built for real shops where staff collect payments and owners are not always present, they eliminate confirmation friction and provide instant payment visibility.

Each Virtual Terminal:

- Has a unique ID
- Generates a dedicated QR code
- Supports multiple payment methods
- Sends real-time WhatsApp notifications
- Tracks transactions per counter or location
- Provides downloadable posters

## Create a Virtual Terminal

<CodeGroup>
```shell cURL
curl -X POST "https://api.modempay.com/v1/virtual-terminals" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Counter 1",
    "whatsapp_numbers": ["+2207012345"]
  }'
```

```ts nodejs
import ModemPay from "modem-pay";

const modempay = new ModemPay("YOUR_SECRET_KEY");

const terminal = await modempay.virtualTerminals.create({
  name: "Counter 1",
  whatsapp_numbers: ["+2207012345"],
});

console.log(terminal);
```

</CodeGroup>

### Parameters

| Field              | Type     | Required | Description                                |
| ------------------ | -------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `name`             | string   | Yes      | Display name for the terminal              |
| `whatsapp_numbers` | string[] | Yes      | Numbers that receive payment notifications |

<div
  style={{
    display: "flex",
    gap: "2em",
    justifyContent: "center",
    margin: "1.5em 0",
    flexWrap: "wrap",
  }}
>
  <img
    src="/images/poster.png"
    alt="Virtual Terminal Poster Example"
    style={{
      width: "100%",
      maxWidth: "340px",
      borderRadius: "8px",
      margin: 0,
      height: "auto",
      objectFit: "contain",
      flex: "1 1 260px",
      minWidth: "220px",
    }}
  />
  <img
    src="/images/poster-2.png"
    alt="Virtual Terminal Poster Example"
    style={{
      width: "100%",
      maxWidth: "340px",
      borderRadius: "8px",
      margin: 0,
      height: "auto",
      objectFit: "contain",
      flex: "1 1 260px",
      minWidth: "220px",
    }}
  />
</div>

These posters showcase a live payment endpoint that is associated with a specific counter or location.

## Retrieve a Terminal

<CodeGroup>
```shell cURL
curl -X GET "https://api.modempay.com/v1/virtual-terminals/f2b9...0243" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>"
```

```ts nodejs
const terminal = await modempay.virtualTerminals.retrieve("f2b9...0243");
```

</CodeGroup>

## Update a Terminal

<CodeGroup>
```shell cURL
curl -X PUT "https://api.modempay.com/v1/virtual-terminals/f2b9...0243" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Main Counter",
    "whatsapp_numbers": ["+220XXXXXXXX"],
    "active": true
  }'
```

```ts nodejs
const updated = await modempay.virtualTerminals.update("f2b9...0243", {
  name: "Main Counter",
  whatsapp_numbers: ["+220XXXXXXXX"],
  active: true,
});
```

</CodeGroup>

### Updatable Fields

- `name`
- `whatsapp_numbers`
- `active`

## List Terminals

<CodeGroup>
```shell cURL
curl -X GET "https://api.modempay.com/v1/virtual-terminals?limit=10&term=Counter" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>"
```

```ts nodejs
const terminals = await modempay.virtualTerminals.list({
  limit: 10,
  search: "Counter",
});
```

</CodeGroup>

## Delete a Terminal

<CodeGroup>
```shell cURL
curl -X DELETE "https://api.modempay.com/v1/virtual-terminals/f2b9...0243" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>"
```

```ts nodejs
await modempay.virtualTerminals.delete("f2b9...0243");
```

</CodeGroup>

## Download Terminal Posters

Each terminal comes with a ready-to-print QR poster.

<CodeGroup>
```shell cURL
curl -X GET "https://api.modempay.com/v1/virtual-terminals/download/f2b9...0243" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>" --output poster.png
```

```ts nodejs
const poster = await modempay.virtualTerminals.downloadPosters("f2b9...0243");
```

</CodeGroup>

Use the downloaded file to:

- Print and display at checkout
- Share digitally
- Place at multiple store locations
